translations.literal: Volume One Hundred Forty
translations.idiomatic: Volume 140

sentences.zh: 【】 ◎齊紀六起旃蒙大淵獻，盡柔兆困敦，凡二年。

translations.literal: Qi Records Six begins at Zhanmeng Dayuanxian and ends at Rouzhao Kundun, two years in all.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Records 6 spans from the year Zhanmeng Dayuanxian through Rouzhao Kundun — two years in all.

sentences.zh: 高宗明皇帝中建武二年（

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianwu of Emperor Ming the High Ancestor (
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianwu of Emperor Ming of Qi (

sentences.zh: 乙亥，公元四九五年）

translations.literal: yihai, 495 CE)
translations.idiomatic: yihai, AD 495)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，壬申，遣鎮南將軍王廣之督司州、右衛將軍蕭坦之督徐州、尚書右僕射沈文季督豫州諸軍以拒魏。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, on the day renshen, they dispatched the General Who Guards the South Wang Guangzhi to oversee Si Province, the General of the Right Guard Xiao Tanzhi to oversee Xu Province, and the Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Shen Wenji to oversee the armies of Yu Province to resist Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the renshen day of the first month, the court sent General Who Guards the South Wang Guangzhi to command the forces of Si Province, General of the Right Guard Xiao Tanzhi to command Xu Province, and Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Shen Wenji to command the armies of Yu Province — all to resist Wei.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，魏詔：「淮北之人不得侵掠，犯者以大辟論。」

translations.literal: On the day guiyou, Wei issued an edict: "The people north of the Huai must not be plundered; offenders shall be judged by the penalty of death."
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou, Wei proclaimed: "The people north of the Huai must not be raided; violators shall face execution."

sentences.zh: 乙未，拓跋衍攻鐘離，徐州刺史蕭惠休乘城拒守，間出襲擊魏兵，破之。

translations.literal: On the day yiwei, Tuoba Yan attacked Zhongli; the Inspector of Xu Province Xiao Huixiu manned the walls to resist, and at intervals sallied forth to strike Wei troops and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei, Tuoba Yan besieged Zhongli. Xu Province Inspector Xiao Huixiu held the city, then made sorties against the Wei army and routed them.

sentences.zh: 惠休，惠明之弟也。

translations.literal: Huixiu was the younger brother of Huiming.
translations.idiomatic: Huixiu was the younger brother of Huiming.

sentences.zh: 劉昶、王肅攻義陽，司州刺史蕭誕拒之。

translations.literal: Liu Chang and Wang Su attacked Yiyang; the Inspector of Si Province Xiao Dan resisted them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chang and Wang Su attacked Yiyang, which Si Province Inspector Xiao Dan defended.

sentences.zh: 肅屢破誕兵，招降萬餘人。

translations.literal: Su repeatedly defeated Dan's troops and induced more than ten thousand to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su repeatedly defeated Xiao Dan's forces and won over more than ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 魏以肅為豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Wei appointed Su Inspector of Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: Wei made Wang Su Inspector of Yu Province.

sentences.zh: 劉昶性褊躁，御軍嚴暴，人莫敢言。

translations.literal: Liu Chang's nature was narrow and irritable; he commanded the army with harsh severity, and no one dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chang was narrow-minded and quick-tempered; he ruled his troops with brutal severity, and none dared object.

sentences.zh: 法曹行參軍北平陽固苦諫；

translations.literal: The acting aide of the Legal Bureau, Yang Gu of Beiping, remonstrated strenuously;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Gu of Beiping, acting aide in the Legal Bureau, remonstrated with him at length;

sentences.zh: 昶怒，欲斬之，使當攻道。

translations.literal: Chang was enraged and wished to behead him, and had him placed on the assault route.
translations.idiomatic: Chang flew into a rage and meant to execute him, but instead sent him to the front of the assault.

sentences.zh: 固志意閑雅，臨敵勇決，昶始奇之。

translations.literal: Gu's will was calm and refined; facing the enemy he was brave and resolute, and Chang came to marvel at him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Gu bore himself with calm dignity and fought with bold resolve; Chang then came to admire him.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，中外纂嚴。

translations.literal: On the day dingyou, within and without the court the guard was drawn up.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, the court and the realm went on full alert.

sentences.zh: 以太尉陳顯達為使持節、都督西北諸軍事，往來新亭、白下以張聲勢。

translations.literal: They made the Grand Commandant Chen Xianda Bearer of the Staff and Commander-in-Chief of all northwestern military affairs, to move between Xinting and Baixia to display martial presence.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Chen Xianda was made Bearer of the Staff and supreme commander of northwestern forces, shuttling between Xinting and Baixia to show strength.

sentences.zh: 己亥，魏主濟淮；

translations.literal: On the day jihai, the Wei ruler crossed the Huai;
translations.idiomatic: On jihai, the Wei emperor crossed the Huai;

sentences.zh: 二月，至壽陽，眾號三十萬，鐵騎彌望。

translations.literal: in the second month he reached Shouyang; the host was said to number three hundred thousand, and iron cavalry filled the horizon.
translations.idiomatic: in the second month he reached Shouyang. His army was said to number three hundred thousand, with armored horsemen as far as the eye could see.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，魏主登八公山，賦詩。

translations.literal: On the day jiachen, the Wei ruler ascended Bagong Mountain and composed a poem.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen, the Wei emperor climbed Bagong Mountain and wrote a poem.

sentences.zh: 道遇甚雨，命去蓋；

translations.literal: On the road he met heavy rain and ordered the canopy removed;
translations.idiomatic: On the march he was caught in heavy rain and had his carriage canopy taken down;

sentences.zh: 見軍士病者，親撫慰之。

translations.literal: seeing sick soldiers, he personally comforted them.
translations.idiomatic: and when he saw sick soldiers, he went among them to comfort them himself.

sentences.zh: 魏主遣使呼城中人，豐城公遙昌使參軍崔慶遠出應之。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler sent a messenger to summon someone from within the city; the Duke of Fengcheng Yaochang sent the aide Cui Qingyuan out to respond.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor sent a messenger to call someone out from the city; Prince Yaochang of Fengcheng sent his aide Cui Qingyuan to answer.

sentences.zh: 慶遠問師故，魏主曰：「固當有故！

translations.literal: Qingyuan asked the reason for the army's coming; the Wei ruler said, "Of course there is a reason!
translations.idiomatic: Qingyuan asked why the army had come. The Wei emperor said, "There must be a reason, of course!

sentences.zh: 卿欲我斥言之乎，欲我含垢依違乎？」

translations.literal: Do you wish me to speak bluntly, or to bear filth and speak evasively?"
translations.idiomatic: Do you want me to speak plainly, or to swallow the truth and hedge?"

sentences.zh: 慶遠曰：「未承來命，無所含垢。」

translations.literal: Qingyuan said, "I have not yet received your command to come; there is nothing to swallow."
translations.idiomatic: Qingyuan said, "I have not yet been told why you summoned me — there is nothing to swallow."

sentences.zh: 魏主曰：「齊主何故廢立？」

translations.literal: The Wei ruler said, "Why did the Qi ruler depose and establish?"
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor said, "Why did your ruler depose one emperor and set up another?"

sentences.zh: 慶遠曰：「廢昏立明，古今非一，未審何疑？」

translations.literal: Qingyuan said, "Deposing the benighted and establishing the enlightened is not unique to our age; what doubt is there?"
translations.idiomatic: Qingyuan said, "Replacing a benighted ruler with a wise one is hardly unprecedented — what is there to question?"

sentences.zh: 魏主曰：「武帝子孫，今皆安在？」

translations.literal: The Wei ruler said, "Where are all the descendants of Emperor Wu now?"
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor said, "Where are all of Emperor Wu's descendants now?"

sentences.zh: 慶遠曰：「七王同惡，已伏管、蔡之誅；

translations.literal: Qingyuan said, "The seven princes shared in evil and have already suffered the punishment of Guan and Cai;
translations.idiomatic: Qingyuan said, "Seven princes shared in treason and have already met the fate of Guan and Cai;

sentences.zh: 其餘二十餘王，或內列清要，或外典方牧。」

translations.literal: the remaining twenty-odd princes either hold eminent posts within the court or govern provinces without."
translations.idiomatic: the other twenty-odd princes either hold honored posts at court or govern provinces abroad."

sentences.zh: 魏主曰：「卿主若不忘忠義，何以不立近親，如周公之輔成王，而自取之乎？」

translations.literal: The Wei ruler said, "If your ruler had not forgotten loyalty and righteousness, why did he not establish a close kinsman, as the Duke of Zhou assisted King Cheng, instead of taking the throne himself?"
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor said, "If your master still cared for loyalty and duty, why did he not set up a close kinsman — as the Duke of Zhou served King Cheng — instead of taking the throne himself?"

sentences.zh: 慶遠曰：「成王有亞聖之德，故周公得而相之。

translations.literal: Qingyuan said, "King Cheng possessed the virtue of a near-sage; therefore the Duke of Zhou was able to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: Qingyuan said, "King Cheng had nearly sage-like virtue, so the Duke of Zhou could serve as his minister.

sentences.zh: 今近親皆非成王之比，故不可立。

translations.literal: Today's close kinsmen are none of them comparable to King Cheng; therefore none could be established.
translations.idiomatic: None of today's close kinsmen measure up to King Cheng, so none could be enthroned.

sentences.zh: 且霍光亦捨武帝近親而立宣帝，唯其賢也。」

translations.literal: Moreover, Huo Guang also set aside Emperor Wu's close kinsmen and established Emperor Xuan — solely because of his worth."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Huo Guang passed over Emperor Wu's kin to enthrone Emperor Xuan — solely because Xuan was worthy."

sentences.zh: 魏主曰：「霍光何以不自立？」

translations.literal: The Wei ruler said, "Why did Huo Guang not establish himself?"
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor said, "Why did Huo Guang not take the throne himself?"

sentences.zh: 慶遠曰：「非其類也。

translations.literal: Qingyuan said, "He was not of their kind.
translations.idiomatic: Qingyuan said, "He was not of their line.

sentences.zh: 主上正可比宣帝，安得比霍光！

translations.literal: Our sovereign may rightly be compared to Emperor Xuan — how could he be compared to Huo Guang!
translations.idiomatic: Our sovereign may be compared to Emperor Xuan — how could he be compared to Huo Guang!

sentences.zh: 若爾，武王伐紂，不立微子而輔之，亦為苟貪天下乎？」

translations.literal: If that were so, when King Wu attacked Zhou, by not establishing Weizi and assisting him instead, was he also greedily grasping the realm?"
translations.idiomatic: By that logic, when King Wu overthrew Zhou, was he also grasping the realm out of greed because he did not enthrone Weizi and serve as his minister?"

sentences.zh: 魏主大笑曰：「朕來問罪。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler laughed loudly and said, "I came to call you to account.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor laughed and said, "I came to demand an accounting.

sentences.zh: 如卿之言，便可釋然。」

translations.literal: With words like yours, I can set my mind at ease."
translations.idiomatic: Hearing you speak thus, I can set my mind at ease."

sentences.zh: 慶遠曰：「『見可而進，知難而退』，聖人之師也。」

translations.literal: Qingyuan said, "'Advance when you see it is possible; withdraw when you know it is difficult' — that is the teaching of the sages."
translations.idiomatic: Qingyuan said, "'Advance when you see an opening; withdraw when you know the odds are against you' — that is the teaching of the sages."

sentences.zh: 魏主曰：「卿欲吾和親，為不欲乎？」

translations.literal: The Wei ruler said, "Do you wish us to make peace by marriage, or not?"
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor said, "Do you wish us to make peace by marriage, or not?"

sentences.zh: 慶遠曰：「和親則二國交歡，生民蒙福；

translations.literal: Qingyuan said, "If there is marriage alliance, the two states will rejoice together and the people will receive blessing;
translations.idiomatic: Qingyuan said, "With marriage alliance, both states will rejoice and the people will prosper;

sentences.zh: 否則二國交惡，生民塗炭。

translations.literal: if not, the two states will turn hostile and the people will be trampled in charcoal.
translations.idiomatic: without it, both states will turn hostile and the people will suffer ruin.

sentences.zh: 和親與否，裁自聖衷。」

translations.literal: Whether there is marriage alliance or not rests solely with your sacred heart."
translations.idiomatic: Whether to seek alliance or not rests solely with your sacred judgment."

sentences.zh: 魏主賜慶遠酒殽、衣服而遣之。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler bestowed on Qingyuan wine, meat, and clothing and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor gave Qingyuan wine, food, and garments, then sent him back.

sentences.zh: 戊申，魏主循淮而東，民皆安堵，租運屬路。

translations.literal: On the day wushen, the Wei ruler followed the Huai eastward; the people all lived in peace at their doors, and rent and transport lined the road.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen, the Wei emperor marched east along the Huai; the people went about their lives undisturbed, and tribute convoys stretched along the road.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，至鐘離。

translations.literal: On the day bingchen, he reached Zhongli.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, he reached Zhongli.

sentences.zh: 上遣左衛將軍崔慧景、寧朔將軍裴叔業救鐘離。

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched the General of the Left Guard Cui Huijing and the General Who Pacifies the North Pei Shuye to relieve Zhongli.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent General of the Left Guard Cui Huijing and General Who Pacifies the North Pei Shuye to relieve Zhongli.

sentences.zh: 劉昶、王肅眾號二十萬，塹柵三重，並力攻義陽，城中負楯而立。

translations.literal: Liu Chang and Wang Su, their host said to number two hundred thousand, with triple ditches and palisades, joined forces to attack Yiyang; within the city they stood bearing shields.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chang and Wang Su, with a host said to number two hundred thousand, threw up triple lines of ditches and palisades and attacked Yiyang together. Inside the city the defenders stood behind their shields.

sentences.zh: 王廣之引兵救義陽，去城百餘里，畏魏強，不敢進。

translations.literal: Wang Guangzhi led troops to relieve Yiyang, but when still more than a hundred li from the city, he feared Wei's strength and dared not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guangzhi marched to relieve Yiyang but halted more than a hundred li from the city, fearing Wei's strength and daring not press on.

sentences.zh: 城中益急，黃門侍郎蕭衍請先進，廣之分麾下精兵配之。

translations.literal: The city grew ever more desperate; the Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate Xiao Yan asked to advance first, and Guangzhi allotted him picked troops from his command.
translations.idiomatic: As the siege grew desperate, Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate Xiao Yan asked to lead the vanguard; Guangzhi gave him picked troops from his own command.

sentences.zh: 衍間道夜發，與太子率蕭誄等徑上賢首山，去魏軍數里。

translations.literal: Yan set out by night on a hidden route, and with the Heir Apparent's aide Xiao Shen and others went straight up Xianshou Mountain, several li from the Wei army.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan marched by night on a hidden route, and with Heir Apparent's aide Xiao Shen and others climbed straight to Xianshou Mountain, only a few li from the Wei camp.

sentences.zh: 魏人出不意，未測多少，不敢逼。

translations.literal: The Wei men, caught unawares, could not gauge their numbers and dared not press them.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei troops, taken by surprise, could not tell how many they were and dared not close in.

sentences.zh: 黎明，城中望見援軍至，蕭誕遣長史王伯瑜出攻魏柵，因風縱火，衍等眾軍自外擊之，魏不能支，解圍去。

translations.literal: At dawn the city saw the relief army arrive; Xiao Dan sent the Chief Clerk Wang Boyu out to attack the Wei palisades, and taking advantage of the wind set fires; Yan and the other armies struck from without, and Wei could not hold and lifted the siege and departed.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the city saw the relief force arrive. Xiao Dan sent Chief Clerk Wang Boyu out against the Wei palisades; they set fires with the wind at their backs, while Xiao Yan and the other columns struck from outside. Wei could not hold and raised the siege.

sentences.zh: 己未，誕等追擊，破之。

translations.literal: On the day jiwei, Dan and the others pursued and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei, Xiao Dan and the others pursued and routed them.

sentences.zh: 誄，諶之弟也。

translations.literal: Shen was the younger brother of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Shen was the younger brother of Chen.

sentences.zh: 先是，上以義陽危急，詔都督青、冀二州諸軍事張衝出軍攻魏以分其兵勢。

translations.literal: Earlier, because Yiyang was critically pressed, the emperor had ordered Zhang Chong, Commander-in-Chief of the military affairs of Qing and Ji Provinces, to lead troops out to attack Wei and divide their military strength.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, with Yiyang in grave danger, the emperor had ordered Zhang Chong, commander of Qing and Ji, to strike Wei from the north and divide their forces.

sentences.zh: 沖遣軍主桑系祖攻魏建陵、驛馬、厚丘三城，又遣軍主僧護攻魏虎阬、馮時、即丘三城，皆拔之。

translations.literal: Chong sent the army commander Sang Xizu to attack the three Wei cities Jianling, Yima, and Houqiu, and also sent the army commander Seng Hu to attack the three Wei cities Huyu, Fengshi, and Jiqiu — all were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chong sent army commander Sang Xizu against the Wei cities of Jianling, Yima, and Houqiu, and army commander Seng Hu against Huyu, Fengshi, and Jiqiu — all six fell.

sentences.zh: 青、冀二州刺史王洪範遣軍主崔延襲魏紀城，據之。

translations.literal: Wang Hongfan, Inspector of Qing and Ji Provinces, sent the army commander Cui Yan to raid Wei's Jicheng and seize it.
translations.idiomatic: Qing and Ji Inspector Wang Hongfan sent army commander Cui Yan to seize Wei's Jicheng.

sentences.zh: 魏主欲南臨江水，辛酉，發鐘離。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler wished to go south to the river's edge; on the day xinyou he set out from Zhongli.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor wished to march south to the Yangzi; on xinyou he left Zhongli.

sentences.zh: 司徒長樂元懿公馮誕病，不能從，魏主與之泣訣，行五十里，聞誕卒。

translations.literal: The Duke of Changle, Yuan Yi, Feng Dan was ill and could not follow; the Wei ruler took tearful leave of him, and after marching fifty li heard that Dan had died.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Yuan Yi of Changle, Feng Dan, was too ill to march. The Wei emperor wept as they parted; fifty li on, he learned that Dan had died.

sentences.zh: 時崔慧景等軍去魏主營不過百里，魏主輕將數千人夜還鐘離，拊屍而哭，達旦，聲淚不絕。

translations.literal: At that time the armies of Cui Huijing and others were no more than a hundred li from the Wei ruler's camp; the Wei ruler took a light force of several thousand men by night back to Zhongli, beat upon the corpse and wept until dawn, his voice and tears unceasing.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Huijing's army was less than a hundred li away, yet the Wei emperor rode back to Zhongli by night with only a few thousand men. He beat upon the corpse and wept until dawn without pause.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，敕諸軍罷臨江之行，葬誕依晉齊獻王故事。

translations.literal: On the day renxu, he ordered all armies to cease the march to the river and buried Dan following the precedent of the Jin Prince Xian of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu he ordered all armies to abandon the march to the Yangzi and buried Dan with the honors accorded Jin's Prince Xian of Qi.

sentences.zh: 誕與帝同年，幼同硯席，尚帝妹樂安長公主。

translations.literal: Dan was the same age as the emperor; in youth they shared inkstone and mat, and Dan married the emperor's younger sister, the Princess Chang of Le'an.
translations.idiomatic: Dan was the emperor's age-mate; they had studied together as boys, and Dan had married the emperor's sister, Princess Chang of Le'an.

sentences.zh: 雖無學術，而資性淳篤，故特有寵。

translations.literal: Though without learning, his nature was pure and sincere, and therefore he enjoyed special favor.
translations.idiomatic: He had little learning, but his character was honest and steadfast, and for that the emperor cherished him above others.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，魏主遣使臨江，數上罪惡。

translations.literal: On the day dingmao, the Wei ruler sent envoys to the river's edge to enumerate the emperor's crimes.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao the Wei emperor sent envoys to the Yangzi bank to recite a list of the Qi ruler's crimes.

sentences.zh: 魏久攻鐘離不克，士卒多死。

translations.literal: Wei had long attacked Zhongli without taking it, and many soldiers died.
translations.idiomatic: Wei had besieged Zhongli for a long time without success, and many soldiers had died.

sentences.zh: 三月，戊寅，魏主如邵陽，築城於洲上，柵斷水路，夾築二城。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day wuyin, the Wei ruler went to Shaoyang, built a city on the islet, palisaded to cut the water route, and built two cities on either side.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on wuyin, the Wei emperor went to Shaoyang, built a fortress on the sandbar, blocked the waterway with palisades, and erected two flanking strongpoints.

sentences.zh: 蕭坦之遣軍主裴叔業攻二城，拔之。

translations.literal: Xiao Tanzhi sent the army commander Pei Shuye to attack the two cities and took them.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Tanzhi sent army commander Pei Shuye against the two strongpoints and captured them.

sentences.zh: 魏主欲築城置戍於淮南，以撫新附之民。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler wished to build cities and post garrisons south of the Huai to pacify the newly submitted people.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor wished to build fortified posts south of the Huai to hold the newly submitted population.

sentences.zh: 賜相州刺史高閭璽書，具論其狀。

translations.literal: He sent a sealed letter to Gao Lu, Inspector of Xiang Province, setting forth the situation in full.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote in full to Xiang Province Inspector Gao Lu under the imperial seal.

sentences.zh: 閭上表，以為：「《兵法》：『十則圍之，五則攻之。』

translations.literal: Lu submitted a memorial, stating: "The Art of War says: 'With tenfold strength, besiege; with fivefold, attack.'
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lu memorialized the throne: "The Art of War says, 'Where you are ten to one, surround; where five to one, attack.'

sentences.zh: 何者國家止為受隆之計，發兵不多，東西遼闊，難以成功；

translations.literal: Why? The state undertook this only for the plan of receiving the abdication; the troops sent were not many, and east and west are vast and distant — success is hard;
translations.idiomatic: The state undertook this campaign chiefly to secure the abdication tribute — not with overwhelming force — and the eastern and western fronts are too far apart to guarantee success;

sentences.zh: 今又欲置戍淮南，招撫新附。

translations.literal: now you also wish to post garrisons south of the Huai and win over the newly submitted.
translations.idiomatic: now you also wish to garrison the Huai south bank and win over the newly submitted.

sentences.zh: 昔世祖以回山倒海之威，步騎數十萬，南臨瓜步；

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Shizu with the might of mountains overturning and seas pouring back, infantry and cavalry in the hundreds of thousands, came south to Guabu;
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Emperor Shizu marched south to Guabu with infantry and cavalry in the hundreds of thousands, his might like mountains overturning and seas rushing back;

sentences.zh: 諸郡盡降，而盱眙小城，攻之不克。

translations.literal: all commanderies submitted, yet the small city of Xuyi could not be taken when attacked.
translations.idiomatic: every district submitted, yet the small city of Xuyi could not be taken.

sentences.zh: 班師之日，兵不戍一城，土不辟一廛。

translations.literal: On the day the army withdrew, not a single city was garrisoned, not a single plot of land was opened.
translations.idiomatic: When the army withdrew, not one city was garrisoned, not one plot of land was settled.

sentences.zh: 夫豈無人？

translations.literal: Was it that there were no men?
translations.idiomatic: Was that because there were no capable men?

sentences.zh: 以為大鎮未平，不可守小故也。

translations.literal: It was thought that the great strongholds were not pacified, and therefore the small could not be held.
translations.idiomatic: No — it was judged that the great strongholds had not fallen, so the small posts could not be held.

sentences.zh: 夫壅水者先塞其原，伐木者先斷其本；

translations.literal: He who dams water first blocks its source; he who fells trees first cuts their roots;
translations.idiomatic: He who dams a river must first block its source; he who fells a tree must first cut its roots;

sentences.zh: 本原尚在而攻其末流，終無益也。

translations.literal: when root and source still stand and you attack the distant branches, in the end there is no benefit.
translations.idiomatic: if root and source still stand, striking at the branches will accomplish nothing.

sentences.zh: 壽陽、盱眙、淮陰，淮南之本原也；

translations.literal: Shouyang, Xuyi, and Huaiyin are the root and source of the Huai south;
translations.idiomatic: Shouyang, Xuyi, and Huaiyin are the root of the Huai south;

sentences.zh: 三鎮不克其一，而留守孤城，其不能自全明矣。

translations.literal: if not one of the three strongholds is taken and you leave men to hold isolated cities, that they cannot preserve themselves is clear.
translations.idiomatic: if you cannot take even one of these three strongholds, leaving men to hold isolated outposts, it is plain they cannot survive.

sentences.zh: 敵之大鎮逼其外，長淮隔其內；

translations.literal: The enemy's great strongholds press them from without, the long Huai divides them within;
translations.idiomatic: Enemy strongholds will press from without, the long Huai will cut them off within;

sentences.zh: 少置兵則不足以自固，多置兵則糧運難通。

translations.literal: with few troops posted they cannot secure themselves, with many troops grain transport is hard to maintain.
translations.idiomatic: too few troops cannot hold the posts; too many make supply impossible.

sentences.zh: 大軍既還，士心孤怯；

translations.literal: Once the great army has returned, the soldiers' hearts are lonely and timid;
translations.idiomatic: Once the main army withdraws, the garrisons will be isolated and afraid;

sentences.zh: 夏水盛漲，救援甚難。

translations.literal: summer waters swell and rise, and relief is very difficult.
translations.idiomatic: summer floods will rise, and relief will be nearly impossible.

sentences.zh: 以新擊舊，以勞御逸，若果如此，必為敵擒，雖忠勇奮發，終何益哉！

translations.literal: Fresh troops striking weary ones, weary troops meeting rested ones — if it truly comes to this, they will surely be captured by the enemy; though loyal and brave they strive, what good in the end!
translations.idiomatic: Fresh troops will strike your weary garrisons; rested enemies will meet your exhausted men. If matters stand thus, they will surely be captured — however loyal and brave, what good will it do?

sentences.zh: 且安土戀本，人之常情。

translations.literal: Moreover, to love one's native soil and cling to one's roots is the constant feeling of men.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, love of home is human nature.

sentences.zh: 昔彭城之役，既克大鎮，城戍已定，而不服思叛者猶逾數萬。

translations.literal: Formerly in the Pengcheng campaign, though the great stronghold was taken and city garrisons were settled, those who would not submit and thought of rebellion still exceeded tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: In the Pengcheng campaign, even after the great fortress fell and garrisons were established, more than tens of thousands still refused submission and plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 角城蕞爾，處在淮北，去淮陽十八里。

translations.literal: Jiaocheng was tiny, situated north of the Huai, eighteen li from Huaiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaocheng was a mere speck north of the Huai, eighteen li from Huaiyang.

sentences.zh: 五固之役，攻圍歷時，卒不能克。

translations.literal: In the Wugu campaign, attack and siege lasted through seasons, and in the end it could not be taken.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wugu campaign, siege dragged on for seasons, and in the end it could not be taken.

sentences.zh: 以今准昔，事兼數倍。

translations.literal: Measuring the present by the past, the affair is several times greater.
translations.idiomatic: Judging the present by the past, the task is several times harder.

sentences.zh: 天時尚熱，雨水方降，願陛下踵世祖之成規，旋轅返旆，經營洛邑，蓄力觀釁，布德行化，中國既和，遠人自服矣。」

translations.literal: The season is still hot, the rains are just falling — I pray Your Majesty will follow Emperor Shizu's established rule, turn the chariot and return the banners, attend to Luoyang, store strength and watch for openings, spread virtue and transform by teaching; when China is at peace, distant men will submit of themselves."
translations.idiomatic: The season is still hot and the rains are coming. I pray Your Majesty will follow Emperor Shizu's precedent — turn the chariot homeward, strengthen Luoyang, husband your strength and watch for opportunity, spread virtue and civilizing influence. When China is at peace, distant peoples will submit of themselves."

sentences.zh: 尚書令陸睿上表，以為：「長江浩蕩，彼之巨防。

translations.literal: The Director of the Masters of Writing Lu Rui submitted a memorial, stating: "The Yangzi flows vast — it is their great barrier.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Masters of Writing Lu Rui memorialized: "The Yangzi flows vast — it is their great barrier.

sentences.zh: 又南土昏備，暑氣鬱蒸。

translations.literal: Moreover, the southern land is dim and damp, and the summer heat steams and swelters.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the southern country is humid and oppressive, and the summer heat is stifling.

sentences.zh: 師人經夏，必多疾病。

translations.literal: Soldiers who pass through summer will surely suffer many illnesses.
translations.idiomatic: Troops who campaign through summer inevitably fall ill in great numbers.

sentences.zh: 而遷鼎草創，庶事甫爾。

translations.literal: Moreover, the transfer of the sacred vessel is newly begun, and all affairs are only just starting.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the move of the capital is still in its infancy, and every branch of government is only just taking shape.

sentences.zh: 台省無論政之館，府寺靡聽治之所。

translations.literal: The terrace and secretariat have no halls for deliberating on government; the ministries and offices have no places for hearing cases.
translations.idiomatic: The central offices have no halls for deliberation; the ministries have no chambers for hearing cases.

sentences.zh: 百僚居止，事等行路，沉雨炎陽，自成癘疫。

translations.literal: The hundred officials dwell and halt as if on the road; soaking rains and blazing sun of themselves breed pestilence.
translations.idiomatic: Officials live like travelers on the road; soaking rains and blazing heat breed pestilence of themselves.

sentences.zh: 且兵徭並舉，聖王所難。

translations.literal: Moreover, to raise both military service and corvée labor together is what even sage kings find difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, to wage war and levy corvée at once is what even sage kings find hard to bear.

sentences.zh: 今介冑之士，外攻寇仇，羸弱之夫，內勤土木，運給之費，日損千金。

translations.literal: Now armored warriors attack the enemy without, while the weak and frail toil at earthworks within; the cost of transport and supply loses a thousand in gold each day.
translations.idiomatic: Now armored warriors fight the enemy abroad while the weak labor on fortifications at home, and transport costs drain a thousand in gold each day.

sentences.zh: 驅罷弊之兵，討堅城之虜，將何以取勝乎！

translations.literal: Driving exhausted troops to attack a foe in stout walls — how will you win!
translations.idiomatic: Driving exhausted troops against an enemy behind stout walls — how can you hope to win!

sentences.zh: 陛下去冬之舉，正欲曜武江、漢耳；

translations.literal: Your Majesty's campaign last winter was meant only to display martial glory on the Jiang and Han;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's campaign last winter was meant only to display martial glory on the Jiang and Han;

sentences.zh: 今自春幾夏，理宜釋甲。

translations.literal: now from spring it is nearly summer — by right you should lay down arms.
translations.idiomatic: now from spring it is nearly summer — by rights you should lay down arms.

sentences.zh: 願早還洛邑，使根本深固，聖懷無內顧之憂，兆民休斤板之役，然後命將出師，何憂不服！」

translations.literal: I pray you return early to Luoyang, make the foundation deep and firm, free the sacred heart from inward-looking worry, let the myriad people rest from axe-and-plank labor, and then command generals to march — what fear that they will not submit!"
translations.idiomatic: I pray you return early to Luoyang, strengthen the foundation, free your mind from domestic worry, let the people rest from corvée, and then send generals forth — who will not submit!"

sentences.zh: 魏主納其言。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler accepted his words.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor accepted his counsel.

sentences.zh: 崔慧景以魏人城邵陽，患之。

translations.literal: Cui Huijing, because the Wei men were fortifying Shaoyang, was troubled.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Huijing was troubled that the Wei were fortifying Shaoyang.

sentences.zh: 張欣泰曰：「彼有去志，所以築城者，外自誇大，懼我躡其後耳。

translations.literal: Zhang Xintai said, "They have the will to depart; they build the city only to boast outwardly and fear that we will tread on their heels.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xintai said, "They mean to withdraw; they build fortifications only to save face and fear we will pursue them.

sentences.zh: 今若說之以兩願罷兵，彼無不聽矣。」

translations.literal: If now we persuade them that both sides wish to cease arms, they will surely listen."
translations.idiomatic: If we tell them both sides wish peace, they will surely agree."

sentences.zh: 慧景從之，使欣泰詣城下語魏人，魏主乃還。

translations.literal: Huijing followed this, sent Xintai to the foot of the city to speak with the Wei men, and the Wei ruler then returned.
translations.idiomatic: Huijing agreed and sent Xintai to parley with the Wei below the walls; the Wei emperor then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 濟淮，餘五將未濟，齊人據渚邀斷津路。

translations.literal: He crossed the Huai; five generals had not yet crossed when the Qi men held the islet and intercepted to cut the ford.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the Huai, but five generals had not yet followed when Qi troops seized the sandbar and blocked the crossing.

sentences.zh: 魏主募能破中渚兵者以為直閣將軍，軍主代人奚康生應募，縛筏積柴，因風縱火，燒齊船艦，依煙直進，飛刀亂斫，中渚兵遂潰。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler recruited whoever could break the Zhongzhu troops to be General of the Direct Gate; the army commander Xi Kangsheng of Dai responded, bound rafts and piled firewood, took advantage of the wind to set fires, burned Qi ships, advanced straight through the smoke, hurled knives in wild cuts, and the Zhongzhu troops then collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor offered the post of General of the Direct Gate to whoever could break the Zhongzhu blockade. Army commander Xi Kangsheng of Dai answered the call: he lashed rafts, piled firewood, set fires with the wind, burned the Qi fleet, charged through the smoke with throwing knives, and routed the Zhongzhu force.

sentences.zh: 魏主假康生直閣將軍。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler made Kangsheng acting General of the Direct Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor made Xi Kangsheng acting General of the Direct Gate.

sentences.zh: 魏主使前將軍楊播將步卒三千、騎五百為殿。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler had the Forward General Yang Bo lead three thousand foot soldiers and five hundred cavalry as rearguard.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor ordered Forward General Yang Bo to command three thousand infantry and five hundred cavalry as rearguard.

sentences.zh: 時春水方長，齊兵大至，戰艦塞川。

translations.literal: At that time the spring waters were just rising; Qi troops came in force and warships choked the river.
translations.idiomatic: Spring floods were rising; Qi forces arrived in strength and warships choked the river.

sentences.zh: 播結陳於南岸以御之，諸軍盡濟。

translations.literal: Bo formed battle lines on the south bank to resist them, and all armies crossed over.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Bo formed battle lines on the south bank to hold them off while the main army crossed.

sentences.zh: 齊兵四集圍播，播為圓陣以御之，身自搏戰，所殺甚眾。

translations.literal: Qi troops gathered on four sides and surrounded Bo; Bo formed a circular array to resist them, fought in person, and killed a great many.
translations.idiomatic: Qi troops surrounded Yang Bo on all sides. He formed a circular defense, fought in person, and killed a great many.

sentences.zh: 相拒再宿，軍中食盡，圍兵愈急。

translations.literal: They faced each other for two nights; provisions in the army were exhausted and the besieging troops pressed ever harder.
translations.idiomatic: The standoff lasted two nights; provisions ran out and the siege tightened.

sentences.zh: 魏主在北岸望之，以水盛不能救，既而水稍減，播引精騎三百歷齊艦大呼曰：「我今欲渡，能戰者來！」

translations.literal: The Wei ruler watched from the north bank; because the waters were high he could not rescue them. Then the waters slightly fell; Bo led three hundred picked cavalry through the Qi ships and shouted loudly, "I wish to cross now — whoever can fight, come!"
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor watched from the north bank but could not rescue them while the waters were high. When the flood subsided slightly, Yang Bo led three hundred picked cavalry through the Qi fleet and shouted, "I mean to cross now — whoever can fight, come!"

sentences.zh: 遂擁眾而濟。

translations.literal: Then he led his host across.
translations.idiomatic: Then he fought his way across with his men.

sentences.zh: 播，椿之兄也。

translations.literal: Bo was the elder brother of Chun.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Bo was the elder brother of Yang Chun.

sentences.zh: 魏軍既退，邵陽洲上餘兵萬人，求輸馬五百匹，假道以歸。

translations.literal: After the Wei army had withdrawn, ten thousand remaining troops on Shaoyang Islet asked for five hundred horses for transport and a passage to return.
translations.idiomatic: After the Wei army withdrew, ten thousand men remained on Shaoyang Islet; they asked for five hundred horses and a passage home.

sentences.zh: 崔慧景欲斷路攻之，張欣泰曰：「歸師勿遏，古人畏之，兵在死地，不可輕也。

translations.literal: Cui Huijing wished to cut the road and attack them; Zhang Xintai said, "Do not block a returning army — the ancients feared this; troops in deadly ground must not be lightly provoked.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Huijing wanted to cut their retreat and attack. Zhang Xintai said, "Do not block a returning army — the ancients feared this. Troops with their backs to the wall must not be provoked lightly.

sentences.zh: 今勝之不足為武，不勝徒喪前功；

translations.literal: To defeat them now would not be enough to count as martial glory; if you do not defeat them you will only waste your former achievement;
translations.idiomatic: Victory would add little glory; defeat would waste all we have won;

sentences.zh: 不如許之。」

translations.literal: better to grant their request."
translations.idiomatic: better to let them pass."

sentences.zh: 慧景從之。

translations.literal: Huijing followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Huijing agreed.

sentences.zh: 蕭坦之還，言於上曰：「邵陽洲有死賊萬人，慧景、欣泰縱而不取。」

translations.literal: Xiao Tanzhi returned and said to the emperor, "On Shaoyang Islet were ten thousand doomed bandits, yet Huijing and Xintai let them go and did not take them.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Tanzhi returned, he told the emperor, "Ten thousand doomed enemies remained on Shaoyang Islet, yet Huijing and Xintai let them go."

sentences.zh: 由是皆不加賞。

translations.literal: For this reason neither received reward.
translations.idiomatic: For this neither received a reward.

sentences.zh: 甲申，解嚴。

translations.literal: On the day jiashen, the alert was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, the realm stood down from alert.

sentences.zh: 初，上聞魏主欲飲馬於江，懼，敕廣陵太守行南兗州事蕭穎冑移居民入城。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the emperor heard the Wei ruler wished to water his horses in the Jiang, he was afraid and ordered Xiao Yingzhou, Administrator of Guangling and acting for Nan Yan Province, to move residents into the cities.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, hearing that the Wei emperor meant to water his horses in the Yangzi, the Qi ruler was alarmed and ordered Guangling Administrator Xiao Yingzhou, acting for Nan Yan Province, to move the populace into the cities.

sentences.zh: 民驚恐，欲席捲南渡。

translations.literal: The people were terrified and wished to roll up their mats and flee south across the river.
translations.idiomatic: The people panicked and prepared to flee south across the river.

sentences.zh: 穎冑以魏寇尚遠，不即施行；

translations.literal: Yingzhou, because the Wei invaders were still far off, did not immediately carry it out;
translations.idiomatic: Yingzhou judged the Wei army still far off and did not act at once;

sentences.zh: 魏兵竟不至。

translations.literal: the Wei army in the end did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: and the Wei army never came.

sentences.zh: 穎冑，太祖之從子也。

translations.literal: Yingzhou was a son of the emperor's younger cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzhou was a cousin of the founding emperor's line.

sentences.zh: 上遣尚書右僕射沈文季助豐城公遙昌守奉陽。

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched the Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Shen Wenji to assist the Duke of Fengcheng Yaochang in defending Fengyang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Right Vice Director Shen Wenji to help Prince Yaochang of Fengcheng defend Fengyang.

sentences.zh: 文季入城，止遊兵不聽出，洞開城門，嚴加守備。

translations.literal: Wenji entered the city, halted roaming troops and would not let them out, opened the gates wide, and strengthened the defenses.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Wenji entered the city, kept patrols inside and barred sorties, threw open the gates as a show of confidence, and tightened the defenses.

sentences.zh: 魏兵尋退。

translations.literal: The Wei troops soon withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei army soon withdrew.

sentences.zh: 魏之入寇也，盧昶等猶在建康，齊人恨之，飼以蒸豆。

translations.literal: When Wei invaded, Lu Chang and others were still in Jiankang; the Qi people hated them and fed them steamed beans.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wei invasion, Lu Chang and other Wei envoys were still in Jiankang; the Qi, resenting them, fed them only steamed beans.

sentences.zh: 昶怖懼，食之，淚汗交橫。

translations.literal: Chang was terrified and ate them, tears and sweat crossing on his face.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Chang ate in terror, tears and sweat streaming down his face.

sentences.zh: 謁者張思寧辭氣不屈，死於館下。

translations.literal: The Herald Zhang Sining's words and bearing did not bend, and he died beneath the lodge.
translations.idiomatic: Herald Zhang Sining refused to yield in word or bearing and died in the guesthouse.

sentences.zh: 及還，魏主讓昶曰：「人誰不死，何至自同牛馬，屈身辱國！

translations.literal: When they returned, the Wei ruler reproached Chang, saying, "Who does not die? How could you make yourself like ox and horse, bend your body and disgrace the state!
translations.idiomatic: On their return, the Wei emperor rebuked Lu Chang: "All men must die — why degrade yourself like an ox or horse and disgrace the state!

sentences.zh: 縱不遠慚蘇武，獨不近愧思寧乎！」

translations.literal: Even if you are not shamed to compare with Su Wu from afar, are you not shamed to compare with Sining nearby!"
translations.idiomatic: Even if you feel no shame beside Su Wu of old, do you feel no shame beside Sining!"

sentences.zh: 乃黜為民。

translations.literal: He was then demoted to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Chang was stripped of rank and made a commoner.

sentences.zh: 戊子，魏太師京兆武公馮熙卒於平城。

translations.literal: On the day wuzi, the Grand Preceptor of Wei, the Duke Wu of Jingzhao Feng Xi, died at Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, Wei Grand Preceptor Feng Xi, Duke Wu of Jingzhao, died at Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 乙未，魏主如下邳；

translations.literal: On the day yiwei, the Wei ruler went to Xiapi;
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei, the Wei emperor went to Xiapi;

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，庚子，如彭城；

translations.literal: in summer, the fourth month, on the day gengzi, he went to Pengcheng;
translations.idiomatic: in summer, the fourth month, on gengzi he reached Pengcheng;

sentences.zh: 辛丑，為馮熙舉哀。

translations.literal: on the day xinchou, he raised mourning for Feng Xi.
translations.idiomatic: on xinchou he went into mourning for Feng Xi.

sentences.zh: 太傅、錄尚書事平陽公丕不樂南遷，與陸睿表請魏主還臨熙葬。

translations.literal: The Grand Tutor and Recorder of the Masters of Writing, the Duke of Pingyang Pi, was displeased with the southern move and with Lu Rui submitted a memorial asking the Wei ruler to return to attend Xi's burial.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor and Recorder of the Masters of Writing Pi, Duke of Pingyang, disliked the southern move and with Lu Rui memorialized asking the emperor to return for Feng Xi's funeral.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「開闢以來，安有天子遠奔舅喪者乎！

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Since the opening of the age, has there ever been a Son of Heaven who ran far for his uncle's funeral!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Since the world began, has any Son of Heaven ever rushed off for an uncle's funeral!

sentences.zh: 今經始洛邑，豈宜妾相誘引，陷君不義！

translations.literal: Now Luoyang is being founded — how can ministers seduce and lead astray, trapping their lord in unrighteousness!
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang is only now being built — how can you ministers tempt me into unrighteousness!

sentences.zh: 令、僕以下，可付法官貶之。」

translations.literal: The Director and Vice Director and below may be handed to the judicial officer for demotion.
translations.idiomatic: Let the Director, Vice Director, and all below be handed to the judicial officer for demotion."

sentences.zh: 仍詔迎熙及博陵長公主之柩，南葬洛陽，禮如晉安平獻王故事。

translations.literal: He still ordered Xi's coffin and that of the Princess Chang of Boling brought south for burial in Luoyang, with rites following the precedent of the Jin Prince Xian of Anping.
translations.idiomatic: He still ordered Feng Xi's coffin and that of Princess Chang of Boling brought south for burial in Luoyang, with the honors accorded Jin's Prince Xian of Anping.

sentences.zh: 魏主之在鐘離也，仇池鎮都大將、梁州刺史拓跋英請以州兵會劉藻擊漢中，魏主許之。

translations.literal: While the Wei ruler was at Zhongli, the Grand General of the Garrison Capital of Chouci, Inspector of Liang Province Tuoba Ying, asked to use provincial troops to join Liu Zao in attacking Hanzhong; the Wei ruler approved.
translations.idiomatic: While the Wei emperor was at Zhongli, Chouci garrison commander and Liang Province Inspector Tuoba Ying asked to join Liu Zao's attack on Hanzhong with provincial troops; the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 梁州刺史蕭懿遣部將尹紹祖、梁季群等將兵二萬，據險，立五柵以拒之。

translations.literal: The Inspector of Liang Province Xiao Yi dispatched his subordinate generals Yin Shaozu, Liang Jiqun, and others to lead twenty thousand troops, hold the passes, and erect five palisades to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Province Inspector Xiao Yi sent generals Yin Shaozu and Liang Jiqun with twenty thousand men to hold the passes and erect five fortified camps.

sentences.zh: 英曰：「彼帥賤，莫相統壹。

translations.literal: Ying said, "Their commanders are base and do not unify with one another.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Ying said, "Their commanders are low-born and do not cooperate.

sentences.zh: 我選精卒並攻一營，彼必不相救；

translations.literal: If I choose picked soldiers and together attack one camp, they will surely not rescue one another;
translations.idiomatic: If I concentrate picked troops on one camp, they will not rescue each other;

sentences.zh: 若克一營，四營皆走矣。」

translations.literal: if we take one camp, the four camps will all flee."
translations.idiomatic: once one camp falls, the other four will flee."

sentences.zh: 乃引兵急攻一營，拔之，四營俱潰，生擒梁季群，斬三千餘級，俘七百餘人，乘勝長驅，進逼南鄭。

translations.literal: He then led troops in swift attack on one camp, took it, and all four camps collapsed together; Liang Jiqun was captured alive, more than three thousand heads were cut, more than seven hundred taken prisoner; pressing the victory he drove far and advanced on Nanzheng.
translations.idiomatic: He stormed one camp and took it; all four camps collapsed. Liang Jiqun was captured alive; more than three thousand were killed and seven hundred taken prisoner. Pressing the victory, he drove on toward Nanzheng.

sentences.zh: 懿又遣其將姜修擊英，英掩擊，盡獲之。

translations.literal: Yi again sent his general Jiang Xiu to strike Ying; Ying made a surprise attack and took them all.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yi sent General Jiang Xiu against him; Tuoba Ying ambushed and captured the whole force.

sentences.zh: 將還，懿別軍繼至；

translations.literal: As he was about to return, Yi's separate army arrived in succession;
translations.idiomatic: As he prepared to withdraw, another column under Xiao Yi arrived;

sentences.zh: 將士皆已疲，不意其至，大懼，欲走。

translations.literal: officers and soldiers were all already weary, did not expect their arrival, were greatly afraid, and wished to flee.
translations.idiomatic: his troops were exhausted, did not expect reinforcements, panicked, and wished to flee.

sentences.zh: 英故緩轡徐行，神色自若，登高望敵，東西指麾，狀若處分，然後整列而前。

translations.literal: Ying deliberately slackened the reins and went slowly, his expression calm; he climbed high to view the enemy, pointed and commanded east and west as if disposing troops, then arrayed his ranks and advanced.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Ying deliberately slowed his pace and kept his composure; he climbed a height, surveyed the enemy, gestured east and west as if deploying troops, then formed ranks and advanced.

sentences.zh: 懿軍疑有伏兵，遷延引退，英追擊，破之，遂圍南鄭。

translations.literal: Yi's army suspected an ambush, delayed and withdrew; Ying pursued and defeated them, then besieged Nanzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yi's army suspected an ambush, hesitated, and withdrew. Tuoba Ying pursued, routed them, and besieged Nanzheng.

sentences.zh: 禁將士毋得侵暴，遠近悅附，爭供租運。

translations.literal: He forbade officers and soldiers from plundering; near and far were pleased and submitted, competing to supply rent and transport.
translations.idiomatic: He forbade his troops from plundering; people near and far submitted gladly and competed to supply provisions.

sentences.zh: 懿嬰城自守，軍主范絜先將三千餘人在外，還救南鄭。

translations.literal: Yi held the city with a tight defense; the army commander Fan Jie first led more than three thousand men outside and returned to relieve Nanzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yi held the city. Army commander Fan Jie, who had three thousand men in the field, marched back to relieve Nanzheng.

sentences.zh: 英掩擊，盡獲之。

translations.literal: Ying made a surprise attack and took them all.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Ying ambushed and captured them all.

sentences.zh: 圍城數十日，城中恟懼。

translations.literal: The siege lasted several tens of days; within the city there was panic and fear.
translations.idiomatic: The siege lasted several weeks; panic spread within the walls.

sentences.zh: 錄事參軍新野庾域封題空倉數十，指示將士曰：「此中粟皆滿，足支二年，但努力堅守！」

translations.literal: The Recording Secretary Army Aide Yu Yu of Xinye sealed and labeled several tens of empty granaries and pointed them out to officers and soldiers, saying, "The grain in these is all full, enough to last two years — only strive to hold firm!"
translations.idiomatic: Recording Secretary Army Aide Yu Yu of Xinye sealed dozens of empty granaries and told the troops, "These are full of grain — enough for two years. Hold firm!"

sentences.zh: 眾心乃安。

translations.literal: The hearts of the host were then calmed.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison's spirits steadied.

sentences.zh: 會魏主召英還，英使老弱先行，自將精兵為後拒，遣使與懿告別。

translations.literal: It happened that the Wei ruler summoned Ying back; Ying sent the old and weak ahead first, himself led picked troops as rearguard, and sent a messenger to take leave of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor recalled Tuoba Ying. Ying sent the weak and baggage ahead, led picked troops as rearguard himself, and sent a messenger to bid Xiao Yi farewell.

sentences.zh: 懿以為詐，英去一日，猶不開門；

translations.literal: Yi thought it a trick; one day after Ying left, he still did not open the gates;
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yi thought it a ruse; a full day after Tuoba Ying left, he still would not open the gates;

sentences.zh: 二月，乃遣將追之。

translations.literal: in the second month he then sent generals to pursue.
translations.idiomatic: not until the second month did he send pursuers.

sentences.zh: 英與士卒下馬交戰，懿兵不敢逼，行四日四夜，懿兵乃返。

translations.literal: Ying and his soldiers dismounted to fight hand to hand; Yi's troops dared not press them; after marching four days and four nights, Yi's troops then returned.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Ying and his men dismounted to fight; Xiao Yi's troops dared not close in. After four days and four nights on the march, they turned back.

sentences.zh: 英入斜谷，會天大雨，士卒截竹貯米，執炬火於馬上炊之。

translations.literal: Ying entered Xiegu; it happened that heaven sent great rain; soldiers cut bamboo to store rice and held torches on horseback to cook it.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Ying entered Xie Pass. Heavy rain fell; his men cut bamboo to hold rice and cooked it by torchlight on horseback.

sentences.zh: 先是，懿遣人誘說仇池諸氐，使起兵斷英運道及歸路。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yi had sent men to entice and persuade the Di of Chouci to rise and cut Ying's supply route and line of retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Xiao Yi had incited the Di of Chouci to rise and cut Tuoba Ying's supply lines and retreat.

sentences.zh: 英勒兵奮擊，且戰且前，矢中英頰，卒全軍還仇池，討叛氐，平之。

translations.literal: Ying drove his troops in fierce attack, fighting as he advanced; an arrow struck Ying's cheek, yet in the end he brought the whole army back to Chouci, punished the rebellious Di, and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Ying fought his way forward; an arrow struck his cheek, yet he brought the whole army safely back to Chouci, crushed the rebel Di, and pacified the region.

sentences.zh: 英，楨之子；

translations.literal: Ying was the son of Zhen;
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Ying was the son of Tuoba Zhen;

sentences.zh: 懿，衍之兄也。

translations.literal: Yi was the elder brother of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yi was the elder brother of Xiao Yan.

sentences.zh: 英之攻南鄭也，魏主詔雍、涇、岐三州發兵六千人戍南鄭，俟克城則遣之。

translations.literal: When Ying attacked Nanzheng, the Wei ruler ordered Yong, Jing, and Qi Provinces to dispatch six thousand troops to garrison Nanzheng, to be sent once the city was taken.
translations.idiomatic: During Tuoba Ying's siege of Nanzheng, the Wei emperor ordered Yong, Jing, and Qi to send six thousand men to garrison the city once it fell.

sentences.zh: 侍中兼左僕射李沖表諫曰：「秦川險厄，地接羌、夷。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant and concurrent Left Vice Director Li Chong submitted a memorial of remonstrance, stating: "Qinchuan is perilous and narrow, its land adjoining Qiang and Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant and concurrent Left Vice Director Li Chong memorialized in protest: "Qinchuan is rugged and borders Qiang and Yi territory.

sentences.zh: 自西師出後，餉援連續，加氐、胡叛逆，所在奔命，運糧擐甲，迄茲未已。

translations.literal: Since the western army marched out, supply and relief have been continuous; moreover the Di and Hu rebelled, and everywhere men race on command — transporting grain and donning armor has not ceased until now.
translations.idiomatic: Since the western campaign began, supplies have flowed without cease; Di and Hu rebels have risen everywhere, and men still race to transport grain and don armor.

sentences.zh: 今復豫差戍卒，懸擬山外，雖加優復，恐猶驚駭。

translations.literal: Now again you pre-assign garrison soldiers, dangling them beyond the mountains; though you add exemptions and relief, I fear they will still be alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Now you propose to post garrison troops beyond the mountains in advance; even with tax relief, the people will be alarmed.

sentences.zh: 脫終攻不克，徒動民情，連胡結夷，事或難測。

translations.literal: If in the end the attack does not succeed, you will only stir the people's hearts in vain; linking with Hu and joining with Yi — the affair may be hard to foresee.
translations.idiomatic: If the attack fails, you will only stir the people in vain and may unite Hu and Yi in ways hard to foresee.

sentences.zh: 輒依旨密下刺史，待軍克鄭城，然後差遣。

translations.literal: I have followed the edict and secretly ordered the inspectors that troops should be dispatched only after the army takes Zhengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: I have secretly instructed the provincial inspectors, per your order, to send troops only after Zhengcheng is taken.

sentences.zh: 如臣愚見，猶謂未足。

translations.literal: In my foolish view, I still say this is not enough.
translations.idiomatic: In my humble view, even that is not enough.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 西道險厄，單徑千里，今欲深戍絕界之外，孤據群賊之中，敵攻不可猝援，食盡不可運糧。

translations.literal: The western route is perilous and narrow, a single path of a thousand li; now you wish to garrison deep beyond the outer boundary, isolated among a host of bandits — if the enemy attacks, relief cannot come swiftly; if food is exhausted, grain cannot be transported.
translations.idiomatic: The western route is a thousand-li single track through rugged country. To garrison deep beyond the frontier, isolated among hostile peoples, is to leave troops beyond swift relief and beyond supply when food runs out.

sentences.zh: 古人有言，『雖鞭之長，不及馬腹。』

translations.literal: The ancients have a saying: 'Though the whip is long, it does not reach the horse's belly.'
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said, 'Though the whip is long, it does not reach the horse's belly.'

sentences.zh: 南鄭於國，實為馬腹也。

translations.literal: Nanzheng for the state is truly the horse's belly.
translations.idiomatic: For our state, Nanzheng is that horse's belly.

sentences.zh: 且魏境所掩，九州過八；

translations.literal: Moreover, the territory Wei covers spans more than eight of the nine provinces;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Wei already holds more than eight of the nine provinces;

sentences.zh: 民人所臣，十分而九；

translations.literal: of the people who submit, nine tenths;
translations.idiomatic: nine tenths of the empire's people already submit;

sentences.zh: 所未民者，唯漠北之與江外耳。

translations.literal: those not yet made subjects are only the north of the desert and beyond the Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: only the northern steppe and the lands beyond the Yangzi remain outside our rule.

sentences.zh: 羈之在近，豈汲汲於今日也！

translations.literal: To hold them in leash when they are near — must you be so urgent today!
translations.idiomatic: Those within reach — must you press them so urgently now!

sentences.zh: 宜待疆宇既廣，糧食既足，然後置邦樹將，為吞併之舉。

translations.literal: You should wait until the borders are already broad and grain already sufficient, then establish states and appoint generals for the enterprise of swallowing and merging.
translations.idiomatic: Wait until our borders are wider and our granaries full, then establish frontier commands and launch campaigns of conquest.

sentences.zh: 今鐘離、壽陽，密邇未拔；

translations.literal: Now Zhongli and Shouyang, close at hand, are not yet taken;
translations.idiomatic: Zhongli and Shouyang, close at hand, are not yet taken;

sentences.zh: 赭城、新野，跬步弗降。

translations.literal: Zhecheng and Xinye — not a step have they submitted.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhecheng and Xinye, the enemy has not yielded so much as a step.

sentences.zh: 東道既未可以近力守，西籓寧可以遠兵固！

translations.literal: The eastern route already cannot be held by nearby force; how can the western frontier be secured by distant troops!
translations.idiomatic: If the eastern front cannot be held with nearby strength, how can the western marches be secured with troops sent from afar!

sentences.zh: 若果欲置者，臣恐終以資敵也。

translations.literal: If you truly wish to post garrisons, I fear in the end you will supply the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: If you truly insist on posting garrisons, I fear you will only arm the enemy in the end.

sentences.zh: 又，建都土中，地接寇壤，方須大將死士，平蕩江會，若輕遣單寡，棄令陷沒，恐後舉之日，眾以留守致懼，求其死效，未易可獲。

translations.literal: Moreover, having established the capital in the Central Land, where territory adjoins enemy ground, you now need great generals and soldiers willing to die to sweep the Jianghui; if you lightly send few and isolated men and abandon them to fall, I fear that when you raise forces again the masses, fearing garrison duty, will not easily give death's effort.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, with your capital now in the heartland, bordering enemy country, you need seasoned commanders and loyal troops to pacify the Yangzi region. If you lightly send a small detachment and abandon it to defeat, I fear that when you next campaign, men will dread being left on garrison duty and will not readily fight to the death.

sentences.zh: 推此而論，不戍為上。」

translations.literal: Reasoning from this, not garrisoning is best."
translations.idiomatic: On these grounds, the best course is not to garrison at all."

sentences.zh: 魏主從之。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler followed it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，魏主如小沛；

translations.literal: On guichou, the Wei ruler went to Xiaopei;
translations.idiomatic: On guichou, Emperor Xiaowen went to Xiaopei;

sentences.zh: 己未，如瑕丘；

translations.literal: on jiwei, he went to Xiaqiu;
translations.idiomatic: on jiwei, to Xiaqiu;

sentences.zh: 庚申，如魯城，親祠孔子；

translations.literal: on gengshen, he went to Lucheng and personally sacrificed to Confucius;
translations.idiomatic: on gengshen, to Lucheng, where he personally sacrificed to Confucius;

sentences.zh: 辛酉，拜孔氏四人、顏氏二人官，作選諸孔宗子一人封崇聖侯，奉孔子祀，命兗州修孔子墓，更建碑銘。

translations.literal: on xinyou, he appointed four men of the Kong clan and two of the Yan clan to office, selected one Kong clansman and enfeoffed him as Marquis Who Revere the Sage to tend Confucius's cult, ordered Yan Province to repair Confucius's tomb, and erected a new stele inscription.
translations.idiomatic: on xinyou, he appointed four members of the Kong clan and two of the Yan clan to office, chose one Kong clansman as Marquis Who Revere the Sage to tend Confucius's cult, ordered Yan Province to repair Confucius's tomb, and erected a new stele inscription.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，魏主如碻磝，命謁者僕射成淹具舟楫，欲自泗入河，溯流還洛。

translations.literal: On wuchen, the Wei ruler went to Que'ao and ordered Gentleman for Appearances and Superintendent of Ceremonies Cheng Yan to prepare boats, intending to enter the He from the Si and return to Luoyang upstream.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen, Emperor Xiaowen went to Que'ao and ordered Gentleman for Appearances and Superintendent of Ceremonies Cheng Yan to prepare boats, intending to enter the Yellow River from the Si and return to Luoyang against the current.

sentences.zh: 淹諫，以為「河流悍猛，非萬乘所宜乘。」

translations.literal: Yan remonstrated, stating that "the river current is fierce and violent — not fitting for the ten-thousand-chariot ruler to ride."
translations.idiomatic: Yan remonstrated, saying, "The river is fierce and violent — not fit for the Son of Heaven to travel."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「我以平城無漕運之路，故京邑民貧。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Because Pingcheng had no route for grain transport by water, the capital's people were poor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Because Pingcheng had no water route for grain transport, the capital's people were poor.

sentences.zh: 今遷都洛陽，欲通四方之運，而民猶憚河流之險；

translations.literal: Now having moved the capital to Luoyang, I wish to open transport from all quarters, yet the people still fear the river's peril;
translations.idiomatic: Now that we have moved the capital to Luoyang, I wish to open transport from all quarters, yet the people still fear the river's dangers;

sentences.zh: 故朕有此行，所以開百姓之心也。」

translations.literal: therefore I make this journey, to open the hearts of the common people."
translations.idiomatic: therefore I make this journey — to open the hearts of the common people."

sentences.zh: 魏城陽王鸞等攻赭陽，諸將不相統壹，圍守百餘日，諸將欲案甲不戰以疲之。

translations.literal: Wei Prince of Chengyang Yuan Luan and others attacked Zheyang; the generals were not unified in command; the siege held over a hundred days; the generals wished to lay aside armor and not fight to wear the enemy down.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Prince of Chengyang Yuan Luan and others besieged Zheyang. The generals were not united in command, and after more than a hundred days of siege they wished to hold their armor and refrain from fighting in order to wear the enemy down.

sentences.zh: 李佐獨晝夜攻擊，士卒死者甚眾，帝遣太子右衛率垣歷生救之。

translations.literal: Li Zuo alone attacked day and night; soldiers dying were very many; the emperor sent Crown Prince Right Guard Leader Yuan Lisheng to rescue them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zuo alone attacked day and night, and very many soldiers died. The emperor sent Crown Prince Right Guard Leader Yuan Lisheng to relieve them.

sentences.zh: 諸將以眾寡不敵，欲退，佐獨帥騎二千逆戰而敗。

translations.literal: The generals, seeing their numbers could not match the foe, wished to withdraw; Zuo alone led two thousand horsemen to meet battle in opposition and was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The generals, seeing they were outnumbered, wished to withdraw; Zuo alone led two thousand horsemen to give battle and was defeated.

sentences.zh: 盧淵等引去，歷生追擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Lu Yuan and others led their forces away; Lisheng pursued and routed them greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yuan and the others withdrew; Lisheng pursued and routed them decisively.

sentences.zh: 歷生，榮祖之從弟也。

translations.literal: Lisheng was a younger cousin of Rongzu.
translations.idiomatic: Lisheng was a younger cousin of Rongzu.

sentences.zh: 南陽太守房伯玉等又敗薛真度於沙堨。

translations.literal: Nanyang Administrator Fang Boyu and others again defeated Xue Zhendu at Shayan.
translations.idiomatic: Nanyang Administrator Fang Boyu and others again defeated Xue Zhendu at Shayan.

sentences.zh: 鸞等見魏主於瑕丘。

translations.literal: Luan and the others saw the Wei ruler at Xiaqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Luan and the others appeared before Emperor Xiaowen at Xiaqiu.

sentences.zh: 魏主責之曰：「卿等沮辱威靈，罪當大辟；

translations.literal: The Wei ruler rebuked them, saying: "You have dampened and shamed our majesty — the crime deserves execution;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked them, saying, "You have shamed our majesty — the crime deserves death;

sentences.zh: 朕以新遷洛邑，特從寬典。」

translations.literal: I, because we have newly moved to Luoyang, specially apply lenient law."
translations.idiomatic: because we have newly moved to Luoyang, I am applying leniency."

sentences.zh: 五月，己巳，降封鸞為定襄縣王，削戶五百；

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on jisi, demoted Luan to Prince of Dingxiang County, reduced households by five hundred;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on jisi, Luan was demoted to Prince of Dingxiang County and stripped of five hundred households;

sentences.zh: 盧淵、李佐、韋珍皆削官爵為民，佐仍徙瀛州。

translations.literal: Lu Yuan, Li Zuo, and Wei Zhen were all stripped of office and nobility and made commoners; Zuo was moreover relocated to Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yuan, Li Zuo, and Wei Zhen were all stripped of rank and made commoners; Zuo was moreover banished to Ying Province.

sentences.zh: 以薛真度與其從兄安都有開徐方之功，聽存其爵及荊州刺史，餘皆削奪，曰：「進足明功，退足彰罪矣。」

translations.literal: Because Xue Zhendu and his elder cousin Andu had merit in opening Xu Region, permitted to keep his nobility and post as Inspector of Jing Province; the rest were all stripped, saying: "Advancing suffices to show merit; withdrawing suffices to display guilt."
translations.idiomatic: Because Xue Zhendu and his elder cousin Andu had merit in opening the Xu region, he was allowed to keep his title and his post as Inspector of Jing Province; the rest were stripped of everything. The emperor said, "Advancing suffices to display merit; retreating suffices to reveal guilt."

sentences.zh: 魏廣川剛王諧卒。

translations.literal: Wei Prince Gang of Guangchuan Xie He died.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Prince Gang of Guangchuan, Xie He, died.

sentences.zh: 諧，略之子也。

translations.literal: Xie He was the son of Lüe.
translations.idiomatic: Xie He was the son of Lüe.

sentences.zh: 魏主曰：「古者，大臣之喪有三臨之禮；

translations.literal: The Wei ruler said: "In antiquity, for a great minister's mourning there was the rite of three imperial visits;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen said, "In antiquity, when a great minister died, the emperor paid three condolence visits;

sentences.zh: 魏、晉以來，王公之喪，哭於東堂。

translations.literal: since Wei and Jin, for princes and dukes' mourning, one wept at the Eastern Hall.
translations.idiomatic: since Wei and Jin times, for the mourning of princes and dukes, the court wept at the Eastern Hall.

sentences.zh: 自今諸王之喪，期親三臨；

translations.literal: From now on, for princes' mourning: for qi-relative kin, three visits;
translations.idiomatic: From now on, for princes' funerals: for relatives in the first degree of mourning, three visits;

sentences.zh: 大功再臨；

translations.literal: for da-gong, two visits;
translations.idiomatic: for the second degree, two visits;

sentences.zh: 小功、緦麻一臨；

translations.literal: for xiao-gong and satin, one visit;
translations.idiomatic: for the third and fourth degrees, one visit;

sentences.zh: 罷東堂之哭。

translations.literal: abolish weeping at the Eastern Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The weeping at the Eastern Hall is abolished.

sentences.zh: 廣川王於朕，大功也。」

translations.literal: The Prince of Guangchuan for me is da-gong relation."
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Guangchuan stands to me in the second degree of mourning."

sentences.zh: 將大斂，素服、深衣往哭之。

translations.literal: When about to enshroud the body, he went in plain garments and deep robes to mourn him.
translations.idiomatic: When the body was about to be enshrouded, he went in plain garments and deep robes to mourn him.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，魏主如滑台；

translations.literal: On jiaxu, the Wei ruler went to Huatai;
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu, Emperor Xiaowen went to Huatai;

sentences.zh: 丙子，捨於石濟。

translations.literal: on bingzi, he halted at Shiji.
translations.idiomatic: on bingzi, he halted at Shiji.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，太子出迎於平桃城。

translations.literal: On gengchen, the crown prince went out to welcome him at Pingtaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen, the crown prince went out to welcome him at Pingtaocheng.

sentences.zh: 趙郡王幹在洛陽，貪淫不法，御史中尉李彪私戒之，且曰：「殿下不悛，不敢不以聞。」

translations.literal: Prince of Zhao Commandery Yuan Gan was in Luoyang, greedy and licentious and lawless; the Censorate Director Li Biao privately admonished him, saying moreover: "If Your Highness does not reform, I dare not fail to report it."
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Zhao Commandery Yuan Gan was in Luoyang, greedy, licentious, and lawless. Censorate Director Li Biao privately warned him, saying, "If Your Highness does not reform, I dare not keep this from the throne."

sentences.zh: 幹悠然不以為意。

translations.literal: Gan was at ease and took no notice.
translations.idiomatic: Gan remained unconcerned and paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 彪表彈之。

translations.literal: Biao memorialized to impeach him.
translations.idiomatic: Biao then memorialized to impeach him.

sentences.zh: 魏主詔幹與北海王詳俱從太子詣行在。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler ordered Gan and the Prince of Beihai Yuan Xiang alike to follow the crown prince to the imperial camp.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen ordered Gan and Prince of Beihai Yuan Xiang alike to follow the crown prince to the imperial camp.

sentences.zh: 既至，見詳而不見幹，陰使左右察其意色，知無憂悔，乃親數其罪，杖之一百，免官還第。

translations.literal: When they arrived, he saw Xiang but did not see Gan; secretly sent attendants to observe his expression, knew he had no worry or repentance, then personally enumerated his crimes, flogged him a hundred strokes, dismissed him from office and sent him home.
translations.idiomatic: When they arrived, he received Xiang but refused to see Gan. He secretly sent attendants to observe Gan's expression and, finding no sign of worry or repentance, personally enumerated his crimes, flogged him a hundred strokes, dismissed him from office, and sent him home.

sentences.zh: 癸未，魏主還洛陽，告於太廟。

translations.literal: On guiwei, the Wei ruler returned to Luoyang and reported to the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei, Emperor Xiaowen returned to Luoyang and reported his return to the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 甲申，減冗官之祿以助軍國之用。

translations.literal: On jiashen, reduced the salaries of superfluous officials to aid military and state expenditures.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, he reduced the salaries of superfluous officials to support military and state expenditures.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，行飲至之禮。

translations.literal: On yiyou, performed the ritual of drinking on return.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou, he performed the ritual of drinking on return.

sentences.zh: 班賞有差。

translations.literal: Distributed rewards in grades.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards were distributed in graded amounts.

sentences.zh: 甲午，魏太子冠於廟。

translations.literal: On jiawu, the Wei crown prince received capping at the temple.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, the Wei crown prince received the capping ceremony at the temple.

sentences.zh: 魏主欲變北俗，引見群臣，謂曰：「卿等欲朕遠追商、周，為欲不及漢、晉邪？」

translations.literal: The Wei ruler wished to change northern customs; he summoned the ministers and said: "Do you wish me to press far after Shang and Zhou, or do you wish me not to reach Han and Jin?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen wished to change northern customs. He summoned the ministers and said, "Do you wish me to press far after the Shang and Zhou, or merely to fall short of the Han and Jin?"

sentences.zh: 咸陽王禧對曰：「群臣願陛下度越前王耳。」

translations.literal: Prince of Xianyang Yuan Xi replied: "Your ministers wish Your Majesty to surpass the former kings."
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Xianyang Yuan Xi replied, "Your ministers wish Your Majesty to surpass the former kings."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「然則當變風易俗，當因循守故邪？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Then should we change customs and transform usage, or follow old ways and keep the past?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Then should we change customs and transform usage, or cling to the old ways?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「願聖政日新。」

translations.literal: They replied: "We wish sagely government renewed day by day."
translations.idiomatic: They replied, "We wish Your sagely rule renewed day by day."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「為止於一身，為欲傳之子孫邪？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Is it only for one person, or do you wish to pass it to sons and grandsons?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Is this only for my own person, or do you wish to pass it to sons and grandsons?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「願傳之百世！」

translations.literal: They replied: "We wish to pass it for a hundred generations!"
translations.idiomatic: They replied, "We wish to pass it down for a hundred generations!"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「然則必當改作，卿等不得違也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Then reforms must be made — you may not disobey."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Then reforms must be made — you may not disobey."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「上令下從，其誰敢違！」

translations.literal: They replied: "When the superior commands, the inferior follows — who would dare disobey!"
translations.idiomatic: They replied, "When the superior commands, the inferior follows — who would dare disobey!"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「夫『名不正，言不順，則禮樂不可興。』

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The saying goes, 'When names are not correct, speech is not in order, then ritual and music cannot flourish.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The Master said, 'When names are not correct, speech is not in order, and ritual and music cannot flourish.'

sentences.zh: 今欲斷諸北語，一從正音。

translations.literal: Now I wish to cut off all northern speech and follow the standard pronunciation alone.
translations.idiomatic: Now I wish to abolish all northern speech and follow the standard pronunciation alone.

sentences.zh: 其年三十已上，習性已久，容不可猝革。

translations.literal: Those thirty years and above have long-established habits — probably cannot be suddenly changed.
translations.idiomatic: Those thirty and older have long-formed habits and probably cannot be changed overnight.

sentences.zh: 三十已下，見在朝廷之人，語音不聽仍舊；

translations.literal: Those thirty and below who are now at court — their speech may not remain as before;
translations.idiomatic: Those thirty and younger who are now at court may not keep the old pronunciation;

sentences.zh: 若有故為，當加降黜。

translations.literal: if anyone deliberately persists, demotion and dismissal should be applied.
translations.idiomatic: if anyone deliberately persists, demotion and dismissal shall follow.

sentences.zh: 各宜深戒！

translations.literal: Each should take deep warning!
translations.idiomatic: Let each take this warning to heart!

sentences.zh: 王公卿士以為然不？」

translations.literal: Do princes, dukes, and ministers think it so?"
translations.idiomatic: Do the princes, dukes, and ministers agree?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「實如聖旨。」

translations.literal: They replied: "It is truly as Your sagely edict says."
translations.idiomatic: They replied, "It is truly as Your sagely edict says."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕嘗與李沖論此，沖曰：『四方之語，竟知誰是；

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I once discussed this with Li Chong; Chong said: 'Of languages from the four quarters, who ultimately knows which is correct;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I once discussed this with Li Chong. Chong said, 'Of all the languages in the realm, who can say which is correct?

sentences.zh: 帝者言之，即為正矣。』

translations.literal: what the emperor speaks becomes correct.'
translations.idiomatic: Whatever the emperor speaks becomes the standard.'

sentences.zh: 沖之此言，其罪當死！」

translations.literal: Chong's words deserve death!"
translations.idiomatic: Chong's words deserve death!"

sentences.zh: 因顧沖曰：

translations.literal: Turning to Chong, he said,
translations.idiomatic: Turning to Chong, he said,

sentences.zh: 「卿負社稷，當令御史牽下！」

translations.literal: "You bear the state — I ought to have the censor drag you down!"
translations.idiomatic: "You bear responsibility for the state — I ought to have the censor drag you down!"

sentences.zh: 沖免冠頓首謝。

translations.literal: Chong removed his cap and bowed his head to the ground in apology.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong removed his cap and bowed his head to the ground in apology.

sentences.zh: 又責留守之官曰：「昨望見女猶服夾領小袖，卿等何為不遵前詔！」

translations.literal: He again rebuked the officials left in charge: "Yesterday I saw girls still wearing crossed-collar narrow sleeves — why have you not followed the prior edict!"
translations.idiomatic: He again rebuked the officials left in charge: "Yesterday I saw girls still wearing crossed collars and narrow sleeves — why have you not enforced the prior edict!"

sentences.zh: 皆謝罪。

translations.literal: All apologized.
translations.idiomatic: All apologized.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕言非是，卿等當庭爭。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "If my words are wrong, you ought to dispute in court.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "If my words are wrong, you ought to dispute them in open court.

sentences.zh: 如何入則順旨，退則不從乎！」

translations.literal: How is it you agree to my face in court yet do not follow when you withdraw!"
translations.idiomatic: Why do you agree to my face in court yet disregard my orders when you withdraw!"

sentences.zh: 六月，己亥，下詔：「不得為北俗之語於朝廷。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on jihai, he issued an edict: "Northern-custom speech may not be used at court.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on jihai, he issued an edict: "Northern-custom speech may not be used at court.

sentences.zh: 違者免所居官！」

translations.literal: Violators shall be dismissed from the office they hold!"
translations.idiomatic: Violators shall be dismissed from the office they hold!"

sentences.zh: 癸卯，魏主使太子如平城赴太師熙之喪。

translations.literal: On guimao, the Wei ruler sent the crown prince to Pingcheng to attend the mourning of Grand Tutor Xi.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao, Emperor Xiaowen sent the crown prince to Pingcheng to attend the funeral of Grand Tutor Xi.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，魏詔求遺書，秘閣所無，有益時用者，加以優賞。

translations.literal: On guichou, Wei proclaimed seeking lost books — those the Secret Archive lacks but useful for the age, richly rewarded.
