translations.idiomatic: On guichou, Wei issued an edict seeking lost books: any not held in the Secret Archive but useful for the age would receive a generous reward.

sentences.zh: 魏有司奏：「廣川王妃葬於代都，未審以新尊從舊卑，以舊卑就新尊？」

translations.literal: Wei officials memorialized: "The consort of Guangchuan was buried at the capital of Dai — it is unclear whether to follow new honor to old low, or old low to join new honor?"
translations.idiomatic: Wei officials memorialized: "The consort of Guangchuan was buried at the capital of Dai. It is unclear whether the new, higher status should follow the old, lower burial, or the old, lower status should be raised to the new honor."

sentences.zh: 魏主曰：「代人遷洛者，宜悉葬邙山。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler said: "Those of Dai who moved to Luoyang should all be buried at Mount Mang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen said, "Those of Dai who moved to Luoyang should all be buried at Mount Mang.

sentences.zh: 其先有夫死於代者，聽妻還葬；

translations.literal: Those whose husbands died first at Dai — permit the wife to return and bury;
translations.idiomatic: Where the husband died first at Dai, the wife may return to bury him there;

sentences.zh: 夫死於洛者，不得還代就妻。

translations.literal: husbands who died at Luoyang may not return to Dai to join their wives.
translations.idiomatic: where the husband died at Luoyang, he may not be taken back to Dai to join his wife.

sentences.zh: 其餘州之人，自聽從便。」

translations.literal: People of other provinces may follow their convenience."
translations.idiomatic: People of other provinces may follow their own convenience."

sentences.zh: 丙辰，詔：「遷洛之民死，葬河南，不得還北。」

translations.literal: On bingchen, an edict: "People who moved to Luoyang who die shall be buried in Henan — may not return north."
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, an edict proclaimed: "Those who moved to Luoyang who die shall be buried in Henan and may not be returned to the north."

sentences.zh: 於是代人南遷者悉為河南洛陽人。

translations.literal: Thereupon all southerners who had migrated from Dai became persons of Henan and Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon all northerners who had migrated south were registered as residents of Henan and Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 戊午，魏改用長尺、大鬥，其法依《漢志》為之。

translations.literal: On wuwu, Wei changed to the long foot-measure and large bushel; the method followed the Han Treatise.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu, Wei adopted the long foot-measure and large bushel, following the standards set out in the Han Treatise.

sentences.zh: 上之廢鬱林王也，許蕭諶以揚州；

translations.literal: When the emperor deposed the Prince of Yulin, he had promised Xiao Chen Yang Province;
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming of Qi deposed the Prince of Yulin, he had promised Xiao Chen Yang Province;

sentences.zh: 既而除領軍將軍、南徐州刺史。

translations.literal: subsequently appointed him General Who Leads the Army and Inspector of Southern Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: but then appointed him General Who Leads the Army and Inspector of Southern Xu Province instead.

sentences.zh: 諶恚曰：「見炊飯，推以與人。」

translations.literal: Chen said angrily: "You see the rice cooking — and push it to someone else."
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Chen said angrily, "You see the rice cooking — and push the pot to someone else."

sentences.zh: 諶恃功，頗干預朝政，所欲選用，輒命尚書使為申論。

translations.literal: Chen relied on his merit and frequently intervened in court affairs; whatever appointments he wished, he would order the Masters of Writing to argue for them.
translations.idiomatic: Relying on his merit, Chen frequently intervened in court affairs; whatever appointments he wanted, he would order the Masters of Writing to argue for on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 上聞而忌之，以蕭誕、蕭誄方將兵拒魏，隱忍不發。

translations.literal: The emperor heard and resented it; because Xiao Dan and Xiao Tan were then commanding troops against Wei, he restrained himself and did not act.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard of this and resented it, but because Xiao Dan and Xiao Tan were then commanding troops against Wei, he restrained himself and did not act.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，上游華林園，與諶及尚書令王晏等數人宴，盡歡；

translations.literal: On renxu, the emperor visited Hualin Garden and feasted with Chen and Masters of Writing Director Wang Yan and several others — full merriment;
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, the emperor visited Hualin Garden and feasted with Chen, Masters of Writing Director Wang Yan, and several others until all were merry;

sentences.zh: 坐罷，留諶晚出，至華林閣，仗身執還入省。

translations.literal: when the seating ended, he kept Chen to leave late; at Hualin Pavilion, personal guards seized him and took him back into the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: when the feast ended, he kept Chen behind; at Hualin Pavilion, personal guards seized him and escorted him back into the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 上遣左右莫智明數諶曰：「隆昌之際，非卿無有今日。

translations.literal: The emperor sent his attendants through Mo Zhiming to rebuke Chen: "At the time of Longchang, but for you I would not have today.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent his attendant Mo Zhiming to rebuke Chen: "At the time of Longchang, but for you I would not be where I am today.

sentences.zh: 今一門二州、兄弟三封，朝廷相報，止可極此。

translations.literal: Now one household holds two provinces, three brothers enfeoffed — the court's repayment can only reach this far.
translations.idiomatic: Now one household holds two provinces and three brothers hold enfeoffments — the court's repayment can go no further than this.

sentences.zh: 卿恆懷怨望，乃雲炊飯已熟，合甑與人邪！

translations.literal: You constantly harbor resentment — and yet say the rice is cooked and the pot should be given to someone else!
translations.idiomatic: You constantly harbor resentment — and yet you say the rice is cooked and the whole pot should go to someone else!

sentences.zh: 今賜卿死！」

translations.literal: Today I grant you death!"
translations.idiomatic: Today I grant you death!"

sentences.zh: 遂殺之，並其弟誄；

translations.literal: Thereupon he killed him, together with his younger brother Tan;
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he had him killed, together with his younger brother Xiao Tan;

sentences.zh: 以黃門郎蕭衍為司州別駕，往執誕，殺之。

translations.literal: He appointed Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate Xiao Yan Acting Administrator of Si Province and sent him to seize Dan and kill him.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate Xiao Yan Acting Administrator of Si Province and sent him to seize Xiao Dan and execute him.

sentences.zh: 諶好術數，吳興沈文猷常語之曰：「君相不減高帝。」

translations.literal: Chen delighted in occult arts and numerology; Shen Wenyou of Wuxing often told him: "Your physiognomy is no less than the High Emperor's."
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Chen was fond of divination and numerology; Shen Wenyou of Wuxing often told him, "Your countenance is no less than that of the High Emperor."

sentences.zh: 諶死，文猷亦伏誅。

translations.literal: When Chen died, Wenyou was also executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Chen died, Shen Wenyou was executed as well.

sentences.zh: 諶死之日，上又殺西陽王子明、南海王子罕、邵陵王子貞。

translations.literal: On the day Chen died, the emperor also killed the Prince of Xiyang Ziming, the Prince of Nanhai Zihan, and the Prince of Shaoling Zizhen.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Xiao Chen died, the emperor also killed the Prince of Xiyang Ziming, the Prince of Nanhai Zihan, and the Prince of Shaoling Zizhen.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，以右衛將軍蕭坦之為領軍將軍。

translations.literal: On yichou, General of the Right Guard Xiao Tanzhi was made General Who Leads the Army.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, General of the Right Guard Xiao Tanzhi was appointed General Who Leads the Army.

sentences.zh: 魏高閭上言：「鄴城密皇后廟頹圮，請更葺治；

translations.literal: Gao Lu of Wei memorialized: "The temple of Empress Mi in Ye City has collapsed — I request that it be repaired;
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lu of Wei memorialized: "The temple of Empress Mi in Ye City has fallen into ruin — I request that it be repaired again;

sentences.zh: 若謂已配饗太廟，即宜罷毀。」

translations.literal: if it is held that she already shares sacrifice in the Grand Temple, then it should be abolished and destroyed."
translations.idiomatic: if she is already deemed to share sacrifice in the Grand Temple, then it should be abolished and torn down."

sentences.zh: 詔罷之。

translations.literal: An edict abolished it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered it abolished.

sentences.zh: 魏拓跋英之寇漢中也，沮水氐楊馥之為齊擊武興氐楊集始，破之。

translations.literal: When Tuoba Ying of Wei raided Hanzhong, Yang Fuzhi of the Zushui Di, for Qi, attacked Yang Jishi of the Wuxing Di and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: While Tuoba Ying of Wei was raiding Hanzhong, Yang Fuzhi of the Zushui Di attacked Yang Jishi of the Wuxing Di on behalf of Qi and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，辛卯，以馥之為北秦州刺史、仇池公。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on xinmao, Fuzhi was made Inspector of Northern Qin Province and Duke of Chouchi.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, on xinmao, Yang Fuzhi was appointed Inspector of Northern Qin Province and enfeoffed as Duke of Chouchi.

sentences.zh: 八月，乙巳，魏選武勇之士十五萬人為羽林、虎賁以充宿衛。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on yisi, Wei selected one hundred fifty thousand brave warriors for the Feathered Forest and Tiger Guards to fill the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on yisi, Wei selected one hundred fifty thousand valiant men for the Feathered Forest and Tiger Guards to serve as palace guards.

sentences.zh: 魏金墉宮成，立國子、太學、四門小學於洛陽。

translations.literal: Wei's Jincheng Palace was completed; the Directorate of Education, the Imperial Academy, and the Four Gates Primary School were established at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Jincheng Palace of Wei was completed, and the Directorate of Education, the Imperial Academy, and the Four Gates Primary School were established at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 魏高祖游華林園，觀故景陽山，黃門侍郎郭祚曰：「山水者，仁智之所樂，宜復修之。」

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen of Wei toured Hualin Garden and viewed the old Jingyang Hill; Gentleman Attendant-in-Ordinary Guo Zuo said: "Mountains and waters are what the benevolent and wise delight in — they should be restored."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen of Wei toured Hualin Garden and viewed the old Jingyang Hill; Gentleman Attendant-in-Ordinary Guo Zuo said, "Mountains and waters are what the benevolent and the wise delight in — they ought to be restored."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「魏明帝以奢失之於前，朕豈可襲之於後乎！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Emperor Ming of Wei lost the realm through extravagance in the past — how could I follow him in the future!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Emperor Ming of Wei lost his way through extravagance before — how could I follow that example after!"

sentences.zh: 帝好讀書，手不釋卷，在輿、據鞍，不忘講道。

translations.literal: The emperor loved reading; he never put down his scrolls — in the carriage or in the saddle, he never forgot to discuss the Way.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor loved reading and never put down his scrolls; whether in his carriage or in the saddle, he never ceased expounding the classics.

sentences.zh: 善屬文，多於馬上口占，既成，不更一字；

translations.literal: He was skilled at composition; much of it he dictated from horseback — once done, not a word changed;
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at literary composition and often dictated pieces from horseback; once finished, he changed not a single word;

sentences.zh: 自太和十年以後，詔策皆自為之。

translations.literal: from the tenth year of Taihe onward, all edicts and proclamations he wrote himself.
translations.idiomatic: from the tenth year of Taihe onward, he drafted all edicts and proclamations himself.

sentences.zh: 好賢樂善，情如飢渴，所與游接，常寄以布素之意，如李沖、李彪、高閭、王蕭、郭祚、宋弁、劉芳、崔光、邢巒之徒，皆以文雅見親，貴顯用事；

translations.literal: He loved the worthy and delighted in goodness, with a hunger like thirst; those he associated with, he always treated with plain sincerity — such men as Li Chong, Li Biao, Gao Lu, Wang Xiao, Guo Zuo, Song Bian, Liu Fang, Cui Guang, and Xing Luan were all cherished for their refinement, rose to wealth and power, and held office;
translations.idiomatic: He loved the worthy and delighted in goodness with a hunger like thirst; those he kept company with he always treated with unadorned sincerity — men such as Li Chong, Li Biao, Gao Lu, Wang Xiao, Guo Zuo, Song Bian, Liu Fang, Cui Guang, and Xing Luan were all drawn close for their refinement, rose to wealth and power, and held the reins of government;

sentences.zh: 制禮作樂，郁然可觀，有太平之風焉。

translations.literal: rites were instituted and music composed — splendid and admirable, with the air of great peace.
translations.idiomatic: rites were instituted and music composed — splendid to behold, with the air of an age of great peace.

sentences.zh: 治書侍御史薛聰，辨之曾孫也，彈劾不避強禦，帝或欲寬貸者，聰輒爭之。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Xue Cong, a great-grandson of Bian, impeached without shunning the powerful; when the emperor wished to show leniency, Cong always contested it.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Xue Cong, a great-grandson of Xue Bian, impeached without shunning the powerful; whenever the emperor wished to show leniency, Cong would argue against it.

sentences.zh: 帝每曰：「朕見薛聰，不能不憚，何況諸人也！」

translations.literal: The emperor often said: "When I see Xue Cong I must feel awe — how much more so for others!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often said, "When I see Xue Cong I must feel awe — how much more so for everyone else!"

sentences.zh: 自是貴戚斂手。

translations.literal: From this the nobles restrained their hands.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the great clans held their hands in check.

sentences.zh: 累遷直閣將軍，兼給事黃門侍郎、散騎常侍，帝外以德器遇之，內心以膂為寄，親衛禁兵，悉聰管領，故終太和之世，恆帶直閣將軍。

translations.literal: He was promoted repeatedly to General of the Direct Gate, concurrently Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate and Regular Palace Attendant; outwardly the emperor treated him for virtue and capacity, inwardly he relied on him as his backbone — the personal guard and forbidden troops were all under Cong's command, so throughout the Taihe era he always bore the title General of the Direct Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through repeated promotion to General of the Direct Gate, concurrently Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate and Regular Palace Attendant; outwardly the emperor honored him for virtue and talent, inwardly he relied on him as his backbone — the personal guard and palace troops all fell under Cong's command, so throughout the Taihe era he always held the title General of the Direct Gate.

sentences.zh: 群臣罷朝之後，聰桓陪侍帷幄，言兼晝夜，時政得失，動輒匡諫，事多聽允；

translations.literal: After the ministers left court, Cong constantly attended within the curtains, speaking through day and night; on gains and losses in current policy he always offered correction — and the emperor mostly approved;
translations.idiomatic: After the ministers left court, Cong constantly attended him within the curtains, speaking through day and night; on the rights and wrongs of current policy he always offered correction — and the emperor mostly heeded him;

sentences.zh: 而重厚沉密，外莫窺其際。

translations.literal: yet he was grave, thick, and deep in reserve — outwardly none could fathom his inner workings.
translations.idiomatic: yet he was grave, steadfast, and impenetrably reserved — outwardly none could fathom his inner mind.

sentences.zh: 帝欲進以名位，輒苦讓不受。

translations.literal: When the emperor wished to advance him in rank and title, he always firmly declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor wished to advance him in rank and title, he firmly declined and would not accept.

sentences.zh: 帝亦雅相體悉，謂之曰：「卿天爵自高，固非人爵之所能榮也。」

translations.literal: The emperor also understood him well in his refined way and said to him: "Your heavenly rank is naturally high — it is truly not something human rank could honor."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also understood him well and said to him, "Your heavenly rank is naturally high — it is truly not something human rank could add luster to."

sentences.zh: 九月，庚午，魏六宮、文武悉還於洛陽。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on gengwu, the six palaces and civil and military officials of Wei all returned to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on gengwu, the six palaces and all civil and military officials of Wei returned to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，魏主如鄴，屢至相州刺史高閭之館，美其治效，賞賜甚厚。

translations.literal: On bingxu, the Wei emperor went to Ye and repeatedly visited the residence of Xiang Province Inspector Gao Lu, praising his governance and bestowing very generous rewards.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu, the Wei emperor went to Ye and repeatedly visited the residence of Xiang Province Inspector Gao Lu, praising his administrative achievements and bestowing very generous rewards.

sentences.zh: 閭數請本州，詔曰：「閭以懸車之年，方求衣錦，知進忘退，有塵謙德；

translations.literal: Lu repeatedly requested his home province; an edict said: "Lu, in the years when he should hang up his carriage, now seeks to return in brocade — knowing advance and forgetting retreat, he has sullied the virtue of humility;
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lu repeatedly requested his home province; an edict said, "Gao Lu, in the years when he ought to retire, now seeks to return home in brocade — knowing advance and forgetting retreat, he has tarnished the virtue of humility;

sentences.zh: 可降號平北將軍。

translations.literal: his title may be reduced to General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: let his title be reduced to General Who Pacifies the North.

sentences.zh: 朝之老成，宜遂情願，徙授幽州刺史，令存勸兩修，恩法並舉。」

translations.literal: An elder statesman of the court should have his wish granted — transfer and appoint him Inspector of You Province, so that encouragement and discipline may both be preserved and favor and law alike upheld."
translations.idiomatic: As an elder statesman of the court, his wish should be granted — transfer and appoint him Inspector of You Province, so that encouragement and discipline may both be preserved and favor and law alike upheld."

sentences.zh: 以高陽王雍為相州刺史，戒之曰：「作牧亦易亦難：『其身正，不令而行。

translations.literal: Prince Yong of Gaoyang was made Inspector of Xiang Province; he admonished him: "To be a regional governor is both easy and hard: If one's person is upright, things proceed without being ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yong of Gaoyang was appointed Inspector of Xiang Province; the emperor admonished him: "To be a regional governor is both easy and hard: If one's person is upright, things proceed without being ordered.

sentences.zh: 所以易；

translations.literal: That is why it is easy;
translations.idiomatic: That is why it is easy;

sentences.zh: 其身不正，雖令不從，』所以難。」

translations.literal: If one's person is not upright, though ordered they will not obey — that is why it is hard."
translations.idiomatic: If one's person is not upright, though ordered they will not obey — that is why it is hard."

sentences.zh: 己丑，徙南平王寶攸為郡陵王，蜀郡王子文為西陽王，廣漢王子峻為衡陽王，臨海王昭季為巴陵王，永嘉王昭粲為桂陽王。

translations.literal: On jichou, the Prince of Nanping Baoyou was moved to Prince of Junling, the Prince of Shujun Ziwen to Prince of Xiyang, the Prince of Guanghan Zijun to Prince of Hengyang, the Prince of Linhai Zhaoji to Prince of Baling, and the Prince of Yongjia Zhaocan to Prince of Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, the Prince of Nanping Baoyou was made Prince of Junling, the Prince of Shujun Ziwen Prince of Xiyang, the Prince of Guanghan Zijun Prince of Hengyang, the Prince of Linhai Zhaoji Prince of Baling, and the Prince of Yongjia Zhaocan Prince of Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 乙未，魏主自鄴還；

translations.literal: On yiwei, the Wei emperor returned from Ye;
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei, the Wei emperor returned from Ye;

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丙辰，至洛陽。

translations.literal: in winter, the tenth month, on bingchen, he reached Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: in winter, in the tenth month, on bingchen, he reached Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，魏詔：「諸州牧精品屬官，考其得失為三等以聞。」

translations.literal: On renxu, Wei decreed: "The provincial governors shall grade their subordinate officials, assess their gains and losses in three ranks, and report."
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, Wei decreed: "Provincial governors shall grade their subordinate officials, assess their performance in three ranks, and report upward."

sentences.zh: 又詔：「徐、兗、光、南青、荊、洛六州，嚴纂戎備，應須赴集。」

translations.literal: Another decree: "The six provinces Xu, Yan, Guang, Southern Qing, Jing, and Luo shall strictly muster military readiness and assemble when required."
translations.idiomatic: Another decree ordered: "The six provinces of Xu, Yan, Guang, Southern Qing, Jing, and Luo shall strictly muster military readiness and assemble when required."

sentences.zh: 十一月，丁卯，詔罷世宗東田，毀興光樓。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on dingmao, an edict abolished Emperor Shizong's Eastern Field and destroyed the Tower of Rising Glory.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on dingmao, an edict abolished Emperor Shizong's Eastern Field and destroyed the Tower of Rising Glory.

sentences.zh: 己卯，納太子妃褚氏，大赦。

translations.literal: On jimao, the crown prince's consort of the Chu clan was received; a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao, the crown prince took Lady Chu as his consort, and a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 妃，澄之女也。

translations.literal: The consort was a daughter of Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: The consort was a daughter of Chu Cheng.

sentences.zh: 庚午，魏主如委粟山，定圜丘。

translations.literal: On gengwu, the Wei emperor went to Weisu Mountain and fixed the site of the Round Mound.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu, the Wei emperor went to Weisu Mountain and fixed the site of the Round Mound altar.

sentences.zh: 己卯，帝引諸儒議圜丘禮。

translations.literal: On jimao, the emperor summoned the Confucian scholars to discuss the Round Mound rites.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao, the emperor summoned the Confucian scholars to discuss the rites of the Round Mound.

sentences.zh: 秘書令李彪建言：「魯人將有事於上帝，必先有事於泮宮。

translations.literal: Secretariat Director Li Biao proposed: "When the men of Lu were about to serve the Supreme Lord, they first had to serve at the Pan Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Director Li Biao proposed: "When the men of Lu were about to sacrifice to the Supreme Lord, they first had to sacrifice at the Pan Palace.

sentences.zh: 請前一日告廟。」

translations.literal: I request that the day before, the ancestral temple be notified."
translations.idiomatic: I request that the ancestral temple be notified one day beforehand."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was followed.
translations.idiomatic: This was approved.

sentences.zh: 甲申，魏主祀圜丘；

translations.literal: On jiashen, the Wei emperor sacrificed at the Round Mound;
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, the Wei emperor sacrificed at the Round Mound;

sentences.zh: 丙戌，大赦。

translations.literal: on bingxu, a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: on bingxu, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 十二月，乙未朔，魏主見群臣於光極堂，宣下品令，為大選之始。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the first day yimao, the Wei emperor received the ministers at the Hall of Glorious Pole, proclaimed the lower-grade ordinance, and began the great selection.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the first day yimao, the Wei emperor received the ministers at the Hall of Glorious Pole, proclaimed the lower-grade ordinance, and inaugurated the great selection of officials.

sentences.zh: 光祿勳於烈子登引例求遷官，烈上表曰：「方今聖明之理，朝應廉讓，而臣子登引人求進；

translations.literal: Director of the Imperial Household Yu Lie's son Deng cited precedent to seek promotion; Lie memorialized: "Under the present sage governance the court should practice humility and yielding, yet my son Deng cites others to seek advancement;
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Imperial Household Yu Lie's son Deng cited precedent to seek promotion; Lie memorialized: "Under the present sage governance the court should practice humility and yielding, yet my son Deng cites others' examples to seek advancement;

sentences.zh: 是臣素無教訓，乞行黜落！」

translations.literal: this shows I have never taught him properly — I beg to be dismissed!"
translations.idiomatic: this shows I have never taught him properly — I beg to be dismissed!"

sentences.zh: 魏主曰：「此乃有識之言，不謂烈能辦此！」

translations.literal: The Wei emperor said: "These are words of discernment — I did not think Lie capable of this!"
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor said, "These are words of discernment — I did not think Yu Lie capable of this!"

sentences.zh: 乃引見登，謂曰：「朕將流化天下，以卿父有謙遜之美、直士之風，故進卿為太子翊軍校尉。」

translations.literal: He then summoned Deng and said: "I shall spread transformation through the realm; because your father has the beauty of humility and the bearing of an upright man, I advance you to Colonel of the Crown Prince's Supporting Army.
translations.idiomatic: He then summoned Deng and said, "I shall spread transformation through the realm; because your father has the beauty of humility and the bearing of an upright man, I advance you to Colonel of the Crown Prince's Supporting Army."

sentences.zh: 又加烈散騎常侍，封聊城縣子。

translations.literal: Lie was further made Regular Palace Attendant and enfeoffed as Viscount of Liaocheng County.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Lie was further made Regular Palace Attendant and enfeoffed as Viscount of Liaocheng County.

sentences.zh: 魏主謂群臣曰：「國家從來有一事可歎：臣下莫肯公言得失是也。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor said to the ministers: "The state has always had one thing to lament: that subordinates will not openly speak of gains and losses — that is the point.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor said to the ministers, "The state has always had one thing to lament: that subordinates will not speak openly of what is right and wrong — that is the point.

sentences.zh: 夫人君患不能納諫，人臣患不能盡忠。

translations.literal: The trouble of the ruler lies in not being able to accept remonstrance; the trouble of the minister lies in not being able to give full loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: The trouble of the ruler lies in not being able to accept remonstrance; the trouble of the minister lies in not being able to give full loyalty.

sentences.zh: 自今朕舉一人，如有不可，卿等直言其失；

translations.literal: From now on, when I raise up a man, if there is anything unsuitable, you shall speak straight of his faults;
translations.idiomatic: From now on, whenever I raise up a man, if there is anything unsuitable about him, you shall speak straight of his faults;

sentences.zh: 若有才能而朕所不識，卿等亦當舉之。

translations.literal: if there is talent I do not know, you also shall recommend it.
translations.idiomatic: if there is talent I do not know of, you also shall recommend him.

sentences.zh: 如是，得人者有賞，不言者有罪，卿等當知之。」

translations.literal: Thus: those who gain men shall be rewarded; those who do not speak shall be punished — you must know this."
translations.idiomatic: Thus: those who gain good men shall be rewarded; those who do not speak shall be punished — you must understand this."

sentences.zh: 丁酉，詔修晉帝諸陵，增置守衛。

translations.literal: On dingyou, an edict ordered repair of the tombs of the Jin emperors and additional guards posted.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, an edict ordered the repair of the Jin emperors' tombs and additional guards posted.

sentences.zh: 甲子，魏主引見群臣於光極堂，頒賜冠服。

translations.literal: On jiazi, the Wei emperor received the ministers at the Hall of Glorious Pole and distributed caps and robes.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, the Wei emperor received the ministers at the Hall of Glorious Pole and distributed caps and robes as gifts.

sentences.zh: 先是，魏人未嘗用錢，魏主始命鑄太和五銖。

translations.literal: Earlier, the people of Wei had never used coin; the Wei emperor first ordered casting of the Taihe five-zhu.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the people of Wei had never used coin; the Wei emperor first ordered the casting of Taihe five-zhu coins.

sentences.zh: 是歲，鼓鑄粗備，詔公私用之。

translations.literal: That year, minting was roughly complete; an edict ordered public and private use.
translations.idiomatic: That year, minting was roughly complete, and an edict ordered their use in public and private commerce.

sentences.zh: 魏以光城蠻帥田益光為南司州刺史，所統守宰，聽其銓置。

translations.literal: Wei made Tian Yiguang, chieftain of the Guangcheng barbarians, Inspector of Southern Si Province; the prefects and magistrates under his command he was allowed to appoint and place.
translations.idiomatic: Wei appointed Tian Yiguang, chieftain of the Guangcheng barbarians, Inspector of Southern Si Province, with authority to appoint and place the prefects and magistrates under his command.

sentences.zh: 後更於新蔡立東豫州，以益光為刺史。

translations.literal: Later Eastern Yu Province was established at Xincai, and Yiguang was made its inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Later Eastern Yu Province was established at Xincai, and Tian Yiguang was appointed its inspector.

sentences.zh: 氐王楊炅卒。

translations.literal: The Di king Yang Jiong died.
translations.idiomatic: The Di king Yang Jiong died.

sentences.zh: 高宗明皇帝中建武三年（

translations.literal: The third year of Jianwu of Emperor Ming the High Ancestor (
translations.idiomatic: The third year of Jianwu of Emperor Ming of Qi (

sentences.zh: 丙子，公元四九六年）

translations.literal: bingzi, AD 496)
translations.idiomatic: bingzi, AD 496)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丁卯，以楊炅子崇祖為沙州刺史，封陰平王。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, on dingmao, Yang Jiong's son Chongzu was made Inspector of Sha Province and enfeoffed as King of Yinping.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, on dingmao, Yang Jiong's son Chongzu was appointed Inspector of Sha Province and enfeoffed as King of Yinping.

sentences.zh: 魏主下詔，以為：「北人謂土為拓，後為跋。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor issued an edict stating: "Northerners call earth tuo and 'after' ba.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor issued an edict stating: "Northerners call earth tuo and 'after' ba.

sentences.zh: 魏之先出於黃帝，以土德王，故為拓跋氏。

translations.literal: Wei's ancestors came forth from the Yellow Emperor; ruling by the virtue of earth, they were therefore the Tuoba clan.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's ancestors came forth from the Yellow Emperor; ruling by the virtue of earth, they were therefore called the Tuoba clan.

sentences.zh: 夫土者，黃口之色，萬物之元也；

translations.literal: Now earth is the color of yellow, the origin of the ten thousand things;
translations.idiomatic: Earth is the color of yellow, the origin of the ten thousand things;

sentences.zh: 宜改姓元氏。

translations.literal: the surname should be changed to the Yuan clan.
translations.idiomatic: the surname should be changed to Yuan.

sentences.zh: 諸功臣舊族自代來者，姓或重複，皆改之。」

translations.literal: Among meritorious ministers and old clans who had come from Dai since antiquity, surnames were sometimes duplicated — all were to be changed."
translations.idiomatic: Among meritorious ministers and old clans who had come from Dai since antiquity, surnames were sometimes duplicated — all were to be changed."

sentences.zh: 於是始改拔拔氏為長孫氏，達奚氏為奚氏，乙旃氏為叔孫氏，丘穆陵氏為穆氏，步六孤氏為陸氏，賀賴氏為賀氏，獨孤氏為劉氏，賀樓氏為樓氏，勿忸于氏為于氏，尉遲氏為尉氏；

translations.literal: Thereupon they first changed the Babo clan to the Zhangsun clan, the Daxi clan to the Xi clan, the Yizhan clan to the Shusun clan, the Qiumuling clan to the Mu clan, the Buliugu clan to the Lu clan, the Helai clan to the He clan, the Dugu clan to the Liu clan, the Helou clan to the Lou clan, the Wunuyu clan to the Yu clan, and the Yuchi clan to the Wei clan;
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon they first changed the Babo clan to Zhangsun, the Daxi clan to Xi, the Yizhan clan to Shusun, the Qiumuling clan to Mu, the Buliugu clan to Lu, the Helai clan to He, the Dugu clan to Liu, the Helou clan to Lou, the Wunuyu clan to Yu, and the Yuchi clan to Wei;

sentences.zh: 其餘所改，不可勝紀。

translations.literal: the rest of the changes cannot be fully recorded.
translations.idiomatic: the remaining changes were too numerous to record.

sentences.zh: 魏主雅重門族，以范陽盧敏、清河崔宗伯、滎陽鄭羲、太原王瓊四姓，衣冠所推，鹹納其女以充後宮。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor greatly valued great clans; the four surnames Lu Min of Fanyang, Cui Zongbo of Qinghe, Zheng Xi of Xingyang, and Wang Qiong of Taiyuan — esteemed by the gentry — all had their daughters taken into the rear palace.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor greatly valued great clans; the four surnames of Lu Min of Fanyang, Cui Zongbo of Qinghe, Zheng Xi of Xingyang, and Wang Qiong of Taiyuan — all esteemed by the gentry — had their daughters taken into the rear palace.

sentences.zh: 隴西李沖以才識見任，當朝貴重，所結姻姻，莫非清望；

translations.literal: Li Chong of Longxi, trusted for talent and insight, was weighty in the present court; every marriage alliance he made was with families of clear reputation;
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong of Longxi, trusted for talent and insight, was weighty at court; every marriage alliance he made was with families of clear reputation;

sentences.zh: 帝亦以其女為夫人。

translations.literal: the emperor also took his daughter as a lady.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor also took his daughter as a lady.

sentences.zh: 詔黃門郎、司徒左長史宋弁定諸州士族，多所升降。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate and Left Chief Clerk of the Secretariat Song Bian to fix the gentry clans of the provinces — many were raised or lowered.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate and Left Chief Clerk of the Secretariat Song Bian to fix the gentry clans of the provinces — many were raised or lowered in rank.

sentences.zh: 又詔以「代人先無姓族，雖功賢之胤，無異寒賤；

translations.literal: Another edict stated: "The northerners who came from Dai originally had no surname clans; though descendants of meritorious worthies, they were no different from the cold and base;
translations.idiomatic: Another edict stated: "The northerners who came from Dai originally had no surname clans; though descendants of meritorious worthies, they were no different from the poor and base;

sentences.zh: 故宦達者位極公卿，其功、衰親仍居猥任。

translations.literal: thus those who rose in office reached the utmost of dukes and ministers, while their meritorious or declining kin still held mean posts.
translations.idiomatic: thus those who rose in office reached the highest ranks of dukes and ministers, while their meritorious or declining kin still held mean posts.

sentences.zh: 其穆、陸、賀、劉、樓、於、嵇、尉八姓，自太祖已降，勳著當世，位盡王公，灼然可知者，且下司州、吏部，勿充猥宮，一同四姓。

translations.literal: The eight clans Mu, Lu, He, Liu, Lou, Yu, Ji, and Wei — from the Grand Ancestor down, their merit shining in the age, their ranks all reaching kings and dukes, clearly evident — shall be reported to the Directorate of the Palace and the Ministry of Personnel: do not fill mean posts with them; treat them the same as the four surnames.
translations.idiomatic: The eight clans of Mu, Lu, He, Liu, Lou, Yu, Ji, and Wei — from the Grand Ancestor down, their merit shining in the age, their ranks all reaching kings and dukes, clearly evident — shall be reported to the Directorate of the Palace and the Ministry of Personnel: do not assign them to mean posts; treat them the same as the four great surnames.

sentences.zh: 自此以外，應班士流者，尋續別敕。

translations.literal: Beyond this, those who should rank among the gentry stream will receive separate edicts in due course.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond this, those who should rank among the gentry stream will receive separate edicts in due course.

sentences.zh: 其舊為部落大人，而皇始已來三世官在給事已上及品登王公者為姓；

translations.literal: Those who were formerly tribal great chiefs, and since Huangshi have had three generations in office at Attendant-in-Ordinary or above, or whose rank reached kings and dukes, are to be surnames;
translations.idiomatic: Those who were formerly tribal great chiefs, and since Huangshi have had three generations in office at Attendant-in-Ordinary or above, or whose rank reached kings and dukes, are to be registered as surnames;

sentences.zh: 若本非大人，而皇始已來三世官在尚書已上及品登王公者亦為姓。

translations.literal: if they were not originally great chiefs, but since Huangshi have had three generations in office at the Masters of Writing or above, or whose rank reached kings and dukes, they are also surnames.
translations.idiomatic: if they were not originally great chiefs, but since Huangshi have had three generations in office at the Masters of Writing or above, or whose rank reached kings and dukes, they are also to be registered as surnames.

sentences.zh: 其大人之後而官不顯亦為族；

translations.literal: The descendants of great chiefs whose offices were not illustrious are also clans;
translations.idiomatic: The descendants of great chiefs whose offices were not illustrious are also to be registered as clans;

sentences.zh: 若本非大人而官顯者說為族。

translations.literal: if they were not originally great chiefs but their offices were illustrious, they are explained as clans.
translations.idiomatic: if they were not originally great chiefs but their offices were illustrious, they are likewise registered as clans.

sentences.zh: 凡此姓族，皆應審核，勿容偽冒。

translations.literal: All these surname clans should be examined and verified — do not permit false claims.
translations.idiomatic: All these surname clans should be examined and verified — false claims will not be tolerated.

sentences.zh: 令司空穆亮、尚書陸琇等詳定，務令平允。」

translations.literal: Order Minister of Works Mu Liang, Master of Writing Lu Xiu, and others to fix this in detail, striving for fairness."
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Mu Liang, Master of Writing Lu Xiu, and others were ordered to fix this in detail, striving for fairness."

sentences.zh: 琇，□之子也。

translations.literal: Xiu was the son of [lacuna].
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xiu was a son of Lu Zhen.

sentences.zh: 魏舊制：王國舍人皆應娶八族及清修之門。

translations.literal: An old regulation of Wei: the household attendants of princely states all had to marry into the eight clans and families of pure cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: An old regulation of Wei held that the household attendants of princely states all had to marry into the eight clans and families of pure cultivation.

sentences.zh: 威陽王禧娶隸戶為之，帝深責之，因下詔為六弟聘室：「前都所納，可為妾媵。

translations.literal: Xianyang Prince Xi took a bondservant household woman as his consort; the emperor rebuked him severely and thereupon issued an edict arranging brides for his six younger brothers: "Those previously taken in from the capital may serve as concubines.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xi of Xianyang had married a woman from a bondservant household as his consort. The emperor rebuked him severely and issued an edict arranging brides for his six younger brothers: "Those previously taken in from the capital may serve as concubines.

sentences.zh: 咸陽王禧，可聘故穎川太守隴西李輔女；

translations.literal: For Xianyang Prince Xi, he may betroth the daughter of Li Fu of Longxi, former Administrator of Yingchuan;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xi of Xianyang may betroth the daughter of Li Fu of Longxi, former Administrator of Yingchuan;

sentences.zh: 河南王幹，可聘故中散大夫代郡穆明樂女；

translations.literal: for Henan Prince Gan, he may betroth the daughter of Mu Mingle of Da commandery, former Palace Attendant of Scattered Duties;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Gan of Henan may betroth the daughter of Mu Mingle of Da commandery, former Palace Attendant of Scattered Duties;

sentences.zh: 廣陵王羽，可聘驃騎咨議參軍滎陽鄭平城女；

translations.literal: for Guangling Prince Yu, he may betroth the daughter of Zheng Pingcheng of Xingyang, Consulting Officer under the Flying Cavalry General;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yu of Guangling may betroth the daughter of Zheng Pingcheng of Xingyang, Consulting Officer under the Flying Cavalry General;

sentences.zh: 穎川王雍，可聘故中書博士范陽盧神寶女；

translations.literal: for Yingchuan Prince Yong, he may betroth the daughter of Lu Shenbao of Fanyang, former Doctor of the Secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yong of Yingchuan may betroth the daughter of Lu Shenbao of Fanyang, former Doctor of the Secretariat;

sentences.zh: 始平王勰，可聘廷尉卿隴西李沖女；

translations.literal: for Shiping Prince Xie, he may betroth the daughter of Li Chong of Longxi, Minister of Justice;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xie of Shiping may betroth the daughter of Li Chong of Longxi, Minister of Justice;

sentences.zh: 北海王詳，可聘吏部郎中滎陽鄭懿女。」

translations.literal: for Beihai Prince Xiang, he may betroth the daughter of Zheng Yi of Xingyang, Director in the Ministry of Personnel."
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiang of Beihai may betroth the daughter of Zheng Yi of Xingyang, Director in the Ministry of Personnel."

sentences.zh: 懿，羲之子也。

translations.literal: Yi was the son of Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was the son of Zheng Xi.

sentences.zh: 時趙郡諸李，人物尤多，各盛家風，故世之言高華者，以五姓為首。

translations.literal: At that time among the Lis of Zhao commandery men of talent were especially numerous; each clan flourished in its family tradition; therefore when the age spoke of eminent nobility, it took the five surnames as foremost.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Li clan of Zhao commandery produced an especially large number of talented men, and each branch flourished in its own family tradition. When people spoke of eminent nobility, they placed the five great surnames at the head.

sentences.zh: 眾議以薛氏為河東茂族。

translations.literal: Public discussion held the Xue clan to be a flourishing clan of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Public discussion held the Xue clan to be a flourishing clan of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「薛氏，蜀也，豈可入郡姓！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The Xue clan are Shu people — how can they enter the commandery surnames!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The Xue are a Shu clan — how can they be entered among the commandery surnames!"

sentences.zh: 直閣薛宗起執戟在殿下，出次對曰：「臣之先人，漢末仕蜀，二世復歸河東，今六世相襲，非蜀人也。

translations.literal: Straight Attendant Xue Zongqi, holding a halberd below the hall, stepped out in turn and replied: "My forebears served Shu in the late Han; for two generations they returned to Hedong; now for six generations we have continued in succession — we are not Shu people.
translations.idiomatic: Straight Attendant Xue Zongqi, halberd in hand below the hall, stepped forward in turn and replied, "My forebears served Shu in the late Han. After two generations they returned to Hedong, and we have now continued there for six generations in succession — we are not Shu people.

sentences.zh: 伏以陛下黃帝之胤，受封北土，豈可亦謂之胡邪！

translations.literal: I submit that Your Majesty is a descendant of the Yellow Emperor, enfeoffed in the northern lands — can you also be called a barbarian!
translations.idiomatic: I submit that Your Majesty is a descendant of the Yellow Emperor, enfeoffed in the northern lands — can you also be called a barbarian!

sentences.zh: 今不預郡姓，何以生為！」

translations.literal: If now I am not included among the commandery surnames, what reason have I to live!"
translations.idiomatic: If I am not now counted among the commandery surnames, what reason have I to go on living!"

sentences.zh: 乃碎戟於地。

translations.literal: He then smashed his halberd on the ground.
translations.idiomatic: He then smashed his halberd on the ground.

sentences.zh: 帝徐曰：「然則朕甲、卿乙乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor said slowly: "Then am I first and you second?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said slowly, "Then am I first and you second?"

sentences.zh: 乃入郡姓，仍曰：「卿非『宗起』，乃『起宗』也！」

translations.literal: He was admitted to the commandery surnames; the emperor also said: "You are not 'Zongqi' but 'Qizong'!"
translations.idiomatic: He was admitted to the commandery surnames. The emperor also said, "You are not 'Zongqi' but 'Qizong' — the one who raises his clan!"

sentences.zh: 帝與群臣論選調曰：「近世高卑出身，各有常分；

translations.literal: The emperor discussed selection and appointment with his ministers, saying: "In recent times high and low origins each have their fixed station;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor discussed selection and appointment with his ministers, saying, "In recent times high and low origins each have their fixed station;

sentences.zh: 此果如何？」

translations.literal: is this really how it should be?"
translations.idiomatic: is this really how it should be?"

sentences.zh: 李沖對曰：「未審上古已來，張官列位，為膏梁子弟乎，為致治乎？」

translations.literal: Li Chong replied: "I do not know whether from high antiquity onward, in spreading offices and arranging ranks, it was for the sons of noble houses, or for bringing order to the realm?"
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong replied, "I do not know whether from high antiquity onward, in spreading offices and arranging ranks, the aim was to serve the sons of noble houses or to bring order to the realm?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「欲為治耳。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "To bring order to the realm."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "To bring order to the realm."

sentences.zh: 沖曰：「然則陛下今日何為專取門品，不拔才能乎？」

translations.literal: Chong said: "Then why does Your Majesty today exclusively take family rank and not elevate ability?"
translations.idiomatic: Chong said, "Then why does Your Majesty today rely exclusively on family rank and not elevate men of ability?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「苟有過人之才，不患不知。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "If one has surpassing talent, one need not fear going unknown.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "If a man has surpassing talent, one need not fear that he will go unknown.

sentences.zh: 然君子之門，借使無當世之用，要自德行純篤，朕故用之。」

translations.literal: But the gates of gentlemen — even if for the moment without use in the age — are after all pure and steadfast in conduct; therefore I employ them."
translations.idiomatic: But the households of gentlemen — even if for the moment they lack use in the age — are after all pure and steadfast in conduct, and therefore I employ them."

sentences.zh: 沖曰：「傅說、呂望，豈可以門地得之！」

translations.literal: Chong said: "Were Fu Yue and Lü Wang obtainable by family station!"
translations.idiomatic: Chong said, "Were Fu Yue and Lü Wang to be obtained by family station!"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「非常之人，曠世乃有一二耳。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Extraordinary men — in a whole age there are only one or two."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Extraordinary men — in a whole age there are only one or two."

sentences.zh: 秘書令李彪曰：「陛下若專取門地，不審魯之三卿，孰若四科？」

translations.literal: Secretary Director Li Biao said: "If Your Majesty exclusively takes family station, do you not consider — which were superior, the three ministers of Lu, or the four categories of disciples?"
translations.idiomatic: Secretary Director Li Biao said, "If Your Majesty relies exclusively on family station, which were superior — the three ministers of Lu, or the four categories of disciples?"

sentences.zh: 著作佐郎韓顯宗曰：「陛下豈可以貴襲貴，以賤襲賤！」

translations.literal: Associate Editorial Director Han Xianzong said: "Your Majesty — can the noble inherit nobility and the base inherit baseness!"
translations.idiomatic: Associate Editorial Director Han Xianzong said, "Your Majesty — can the noble inherit nobility and the base inherit baseness!"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「必有高明卓然、出類拔萃者，朕亦不拘此制。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "There will surely be those lofty and outstanding, surpassing the common run — I also do not bind them with this regulation."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "There will surely be men lofty and outstanding, surpassing the common run — I also do not bind them with this regulation."

sentences.zh: 頃之，劉昶入朝，帝謂昶曰：「或言唯能是寄，不必拘門；

translations.literal: Before long Liu Chang entered court; the emperor said to Chang: "Some say that only ability should be entrusted to office, without need to be bound by family gates;
translations.idiomatic: Before long Liu Chang entered court. The emperor said to him, "Some say that office should be entrusted only to ability, without need to be bound by family gates;

sentences.zh: 朕以為不爾。

translations.literal: I believe it is not so.
translations.idiomatic: I do not believe that.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 清濁同流，混齊一等，君子小人，名品無別，此殊為不可。

translations.literal: Clear and turbid flowing together, mixed into one level, gentleman and petty man with no distinction in name and rank — this is utterly unacceptable.
translations.idiomatic: For the clear and the turbid to flow together, mixed into one level, with gentleman and petty man undistinguished in name and rank — that is utterly unacceptable.

sentences.zh: 我今八族以上士人，品第有九，九品之外，小人之官復有七等。

translations.literal: I now have nine grades for shi above the eight clans; beyond the nine grades, petty men's offices have seven additional ranks.
translations.idiomatic: I now have nine grades for gentlemen of the eight clans and above; beyond the nine grades, the offices of petty men have seven additional ranks.

sentences.zh: 若有其人，可起家為三公。

translations.literal: If there is such a man, he may rise from humble origin to the Three Ducal Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: If such a man exists, he may rise from humble origin to one of the Three Ducal Ministers.

sentences.zh: 正恐賢才難得，不可止為一人渾我典制也。」

translations.literal: I only fear that talent is hard to obtain — one must not overturn my regulations for a single person."
translations.idiomatic: I only fear that talent is hard to find — one must not overturn my whole system of regulations for a single man."

sentences.zh: 臣光曰：「選舉之法，先門地而後賢才，此魏、晉之深弊，而歷代相因，莫之能改也。

translations.literal: Your servant Guang says: "The method of selection, putting family station before talent — this was the deep flaw of Wei and Jin, yet dynasty after dynasty inherited it and none could reform it.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang remarks: "The method of selection, putting family station before talent, was the deep flaw of Wei and Jin; yet dynasty after dynasty inherited it, and none could reform it.

sentences.zh: 夫君子、小人，不在於世祿與側微。

translations.literal: Gentleman and petty man do not depend on hereditary emolument versus humble origin.
translations.idiomatic: Whether a man is a gentleman or a petty man does not depend on hereditary emolument or humble origin.

sentences.zh: 以今日視之，愚智所同知也。

translations.literal: Viewed from today, foolish and wise alike know this.
translations.idiomatic: Viewed from our own day, both the foolish and the wise know this.

sentences.zh: 當是之時，雖魏孝文之賢，猶不免斯蔽。

translations.literal: At that time, even the worth of Emperor Xiaowen of Wei could not avoid this blindness.
translations.idiomatic: Even in that age, for all the worth of Emperor Xiaowen of Wei, he could not escape this blindness.

sentences.zh: 故夫明辨是非而不惑於世俗者，誠鮮矣！」

translations.literal: Therefore those who discern right and wrong and are not deluded by the age — how rare they truly are!"
translations.idiomatic: How rare, then, are those who discern right and wrong and are not deluded by the customs of their age!"

sentences.zh: 壬辰，魏徒始平王勰為彭城王，復定襄縣王鸞為城陽王。

translations.literal: On renchen, Wei transferred Shiping Prince Xie to be Prince of Pengcheng, and restored Prince Luan of Dingxiang county as Prince of Chengyang.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, Wei transferred Prince Xie of Shiping to Prince of Pengcheng and restored Prince Luan of Dingxiang county as Prince of Chengyang.

sentences.zh: 二月，壬寅，魏詔：「君臣自非金革，聽終三年喪。」

translations.literal: In the second month, on renyin, Wei proclaimed: "Lord and minister, unless under arms and armor, may complete the three-year mourning."
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on renyin, Wei proclaimed: "Unless under arms, lords and ministers may complete the full three-year mourning period."

sentences.zh: 丙午，魏詔：「畿內七十已上，暮春赴京師行養老之禮。」

translations.literal: On bingwu, Wei proclaimed: "Those seventy and above within the capital region, in late spring shall go to the capital to perform the rites of encouraging the elderly."
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, Wei proclaimed: "Those seventy and above within the capital region shall, in late spring, go to the capital to perform the rites of encouraging the elderly."

sentences.zh: 三月，丙寅，宴群臣及國老、庶老於華林園。

translations.literal: In the third month, on bingyin, he feasted the ministers together with state elders and common elders in Hualin Garden.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on bingyin, he feasted his ministers together with state elders and common elders in Hualin Garden.

sentences.zh: 詔：「國老，黃耇已上，假中散大夫、郡守；

translations.literal: An edict stated: "State elders, those of yellow hoar and above, are granted acting Palace Attendant of Scattered Duties or commandery governor;
translations.idiomatic: An edict stated: "State elders — those of yellow hoar and above — are granted acting Palace Attendant of Scattered Duties or the post of commandery governor;

sentences.zh: 耆年已上，假給事中、縣令。

translations.literal: those of venerable age and above, acting Palace Attendant or county magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: those of venerable age and above are granted acting Palace Attendant or county magistrate.

sentences.zh: 庶老，直假郡、縣，各賜鳩杖、衣裳。」

translations.literal: Common elders are directly granted commandery and county posts; each is given a dove staff and clothing."
translations.idiomatic: Common elders are directly granted commandery and county posts; each is given a dove staff and clothing."

sentences.zh: 丁丑，魏詔：「諸州中正各舉其鄉民望，年五十已上守素衡門者，授以令、長。」

translations.literal: On dingchou, Wei proclaimed: "Each provincial zhongzheng shall recommend men of local renown in his district, age fifty and above, of unblemished integrity and closed gates, and appoint them as magistrate and elder."
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou, Wei proclaimed: "Each provincial zhongzheng shall recommend men of local renown in his district who are fifty or older, of unblemished integrity and closed gates, and appoint them as magistrate or elder."

sentences.zh: 壬午，詔：「乘輿有金銀飾校者，皆剔除之。」

translations.literal: On renwu, an edict stated: "Wherever the imperial carriage has gold and silver ornamental fittings, all are to be removed."
translations.idiomatic: On renwu, an edict stated: "Wherever the imperial carriage bears gold or silver ornamental fittings, they are all to be removed."

sentences.zh: 上志慕節儉。

translations.literal: The emperor admired and emulated thrift.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor admired and emulated thrift.

sentences.zh: 太官嘗進裹蒸，上曰：「我食此不盡，可四破之，餘充晚食。」

translations.literal: The Imperial Kitchen once presented wrapped steam buns; the emperor said: "I cannot finish eating this — it may be broken into four parts; the remainder will serve for the evening meal."
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Kitchen once presented wrapped steamed buns. The emperor said, "I cannot finish this — break it into four parts; the remainder will serve for my evening meal."

sentences.zh: 又嘗用皁莢，以餘濼授左右曰：「此可更用。」

translations.literal: He also once used black-pod soap; he gave the remaining solution to his attendants, saying: "This can be used again."
translations.idiomatic: He also once used black-pod soap and gave the remaining solution to his attendants, saying, "This can be used again."

sentences.zh: 太官元日上壽，有銀酒鎗，上欲壞之；

translations.literal: On New Year's Day the Imperial Kitchen offered longevity wine with a silver wine flagon; the emperor wished to destroy it;
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day the Imperial Kitchen offered longevity wine in a silver flagon, and the emperor wished to destroy it;

sentences.zh: 王晏等咸稱盛德，衛尉蕭穎冑曰：「朝廷盛禮，莫若三元。

translations.literal: Wang Yan and the others all praised his sagely virtue; Commandant of the Guard Xiao Yingzhou said: "Of the court's grand ceremonies, none surpass the Three Origins.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan and the others all praised his sagely virtue, but Commandant of the Guard Xiao Yingzhou said, "Of the court's grand ceremonies, none surpass the Three Origins.

sentences.zh: 此一器既是舊物，不足為侈。」

translations.literal: This single vessel being an old piece is not enough to count as extravagance."
translations.idiomatic: This single vessel is an old piece and is not enough to count as extravagance."

sentences.zh: 上不悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 後預曲宴，銀器滿席。

translations.literal: Later, at a private feast, silver vessels filled the table.
translations.idiomatic: Later, at a private feast, silver vessels filled the table.

sentences.zh: 穎冑曰：「陛下前欲壞酒金倉，恐宜移在此器。」

translations.literal: Yingzhou said: "Your Majesty previously wished to destroy the gold wine store — I fear it should have been moved to these vessels."
translations.idiomatic: Yingzhou said, "Your Majesty previously wished to destroy the gold wine store — I fear it should have been moved to these vessels instead."

sentences.zh: 上甚慚。

translations.literal: The emperor was deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply ashamed.

sentences.zh: 上躬親細務，綱目亦密，於是郡縣及六署、九府常行職事，莫不啟聞，取決詔敕。

translations.literal: The emperor personally attended to minute affairs; regulations were also dense; thereupon in commanderies and counties and the six directorates and nine offices, for routine duties none failed to report and seek decisions from edicts and decrees.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally attended to minute affairs, and his regulations were also dense. Thereupon in the commanderies and counties, the six directorates, and the nine offices, none of the routine duties failed to be reported upward for decision by edict and decree.

sentences.zh: 文武勳舊，皆不歸選部，親近憑勢，戶相通進，人群之務過繁密。

translations.literal: Civil and military men of merit and long service did not go through the Selection Department; intimate followers relied on influence, households mutually pushed advancement — the duties of the masses became excessively dense.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military men of merit and long service did not pass through the Selection Department; intimate followers relied on influence, and households pushed one another forward in office — the business of the realm grew excessively dense.

sentences.zh: 南康王侍郎穎川鐘嶸上書言：「古者，明君揆才頒政，量能授職，三公坐而論道，九卿作而成務，天子唯恭己南面而已。」

translations.literal: Attendant of the Prince of Nan Kang, Zhong Rong of Yingchuan, memorialized, saying: "In antiquity, enlightened rulers measured talent to issue government, gauged capacity to assign office; the three dukes sat discussing the Way, the nine ministers completed the tasks, and the Son of Heaven only respectfully faced south."
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Rong of Yingchuan, attendant to the Prince of Nan Kang, memorialized, saying, "In antiquity enlightened rulers measured talent to issue government and gauged capacity to assign office. The three dukes sat discussing the Way, the nine ministers completed the tasks, and the Son of Heaven only respectfully faced south."

sentences.zh: 書奏，上不懌，謂太中大夫顧暠曰：「鐘嶸何人，欲斷朕機務！

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor was displeased and said to Grand Master of the Court Gu Hao: "Who is Zhong Rong, that he wishes to cut off my affairs!
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor was displeased and said to Grand Master of the Court Gu Hao, "Who is this Zhong Rong, that he wishes to cut me off from my affairs!

sentences.zh: 卿識之不？」

translations.literal: Do you know him?"
translations.idiomatic: Do you know him?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「嶸雖位末名卑，而所言或有可采。

translations.literal: He replied: "Although Rong is low in rank and obscure in name, what he said may have something worth adopting.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Although Rong is low in rank and obscure in name, what he said may have something worth adopting.

sentences.zh: 且繁碎職事，各有司存；

translations.literal: Moreover, tedious and minute duties each have their departments;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, tedious and minute duties each have their departments;

sentences.zh: 今人主總而親之，是人主愈勞而人臣愈逸，所謂『代包人宰而為大匠斫』也。」

translations.literal: when the lord personally oversees them all, the lord grows more weary and the ministers more at ease — what is called 'replacing the people's steward and acting as the great craftsman hewing wood.'"
translations.idiomatic: when the lord personally oversees them all, the lord grows more weary and the ministers more at ease — what is called 'replacing the people's steward and acting as the great craftsman hewing wood himself.'"

sentences.zh: 上不顧而言他。

translations.literal: The emperor paid no heed and spoke of other things.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor paid no heed and spoke of other things.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，甲辰，魏廣州刺史薛法護來降。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on jiachen, Xue Fahu, Inspector of Guangzhou in Wei, came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on jiachen, Xue Fahu, Inspector of Guangzhou in Wei, came to surrender.

sentences.zh: 魏寇司州，櫟城戍主魏僧鈱拒破之。

translations.literal: Wei raided Si Province; Wei Sengyin, garrison commander of Liyang city, repulsed and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Wei raided Si Province, but Wei Sengyin, garrison commander of Liyang, repulsed and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 五月，丙戌，魏營方澤於河陰。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on bingxu, Wei constructed the suburban altar at Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on bingxu, Wei constructed the suburban altar at Heyin.

sentences.zh: 又詔漢、魏、晉諸帝陵，百步內禁樵蘇。

translations.literal: An edict also forbade gathering firewood within a hundred paces of the tombs of the emperors of Han, Wei, and Jin.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also forbade gathering firewood within a hundred paces of the tombs of the emperors of Han, Wei, and Jin.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，魏主有事於方澤。

translations.literal: On dinghai, the Wei ruler performed the rites at the suburban altar.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, the Wei ruler performed the rites at the suburban altar.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，魏廢皇后馮氏。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Wei deposed Empress Feng.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Wei deposed Empress Feng.

sentences.zh: 初，文明太后欲其家貴重，簡馮熙二女入掖庭，其一早卒，其一得幸於魏主，未幾，有疾，還家為尼。

translations.literal: Initially Empress Dowager Wencheng wished her family to be elevated in honor; she selected two daughters of Feng Xi for the rear palace; one died early, one gained the Wei ruler's favor; before long she fell ill and returned home as a nun.
translations.idiomatic: Initially Empress Dowager Wencheng wished to elevate her family's honor and selected two daughters of Feng Xi for the rear palace. One died early; the other won the Wei ruler's favor, but before long she fell ill and returned home to become a nun.

sentences.zh: 及太后殂，帝立熙少女為皇后。

translations.literal: When the dowager died, the emperor installed Xi's younger daughter as empress.
translations.idiomatic: When the dowager died, the emperor installed Xi's younger daughter as empress.

sentences.zh: 既而其姊疾愈，帝思之，復迎入宮，拜左昭儀；

translations.literal: Afterwards her elder sister's illness healed; the emperor missed her and welcomed her back into the palace, appointing her Left Worthy Lady;
translations.idiomatic: Afterwards her elder sister recovered from her illness. The emperor missed her and welcomed her back into the palace, appointing her Left Worthy Lady;

sentences.zh: 後寵浸衰。

translations.literal: later the empress's favor gradually waned.
translations.idiomatic: but the empress's favor gradually waned.

sentences.zh: 昭儀自以年長，且先入宮，不率妾禮。

translations.literal: The Worthy Lady, considering herself older and having entered the palace first, did not observe concubine decorum.
translations.idiomatic: The Worthy Lady, considering herself older and having entered the palace first, did not observe the decorum owed a concubine.

sentences.zh: 後頗愧恨，歸儀因譖而廢之。

translations.literal: The empress grew resentful; through slander in the name of ritual propriety she was deposed.
translations.idiomatic: The empress grew resentful, and through slander couched in the language of ritual propriety she was deposed.

sentences.zh: 後素有德操，遂居瑤光寺為練行尼。

translations.literal: The empress had always possessed moral conduct; thereupon she resided at Yaoguang Temple as a practicing nun.
translations.idiomatic: The empress had always possessed moral conduct; thereupon she took up residence at Yaoguang Temple as a practicing nun.

sentences.zh: 魏主以久旱，自癸未不食至於乙酉，群臣皆詣中書省請見。

translations.literal: Because of prolonged drought, the Wei ruler from guiwei abstained from food until yiyou; the ministers all went to the Secretariat requesting an audience.
translations.idiomatic: Because of prolonged drought, the Wei ruler abstained from food from guiwei until yiyou, and the ministers all went to the Secretariat to request an audience.

sentences.zh: 帝在崇虎樓，遣舍人辭焉，且問來故。

translations.literal: The emperor was at Chonghu Tower; he sent a palace attendant to decline and also to ask their reason for coming.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was at Chonghu Tower. He sent a palace attendant to decline the audience and also to ask why they had come.

sentences.zh: 豫州刺史王肅對曰：「今四效雨已沾洽，獨京城微少。

translations.literal: Yuzhou Inspector Wang Su replied: "Now rain in the four quarters has already soaked through; only the capital is slightly less.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhou Inspector Wang Su replied, "Rain has already soaked the four quarters; only the capital has received somewhat less.

sentences.zh: 庶民未乏一餐而陛下輟膳三日，臣下惶惶，無復情地。」

translations.literal: The common people are not lacking a meal, yet Your Majesty has stopped eating for three days — your subordinates are anxious and have no place for feeling."
translations.idiomatic: The common people are not yet lacking a meal, yet Your Majesty has stopped eating for three days. Your subordinates are anxious beyond bearing."

sentences.zh: 帝使舍人應之曰：「朕不食數日，猶無所感。

translations.literal: The emperor had the attendant reply: "I have not eaten for many days, yet still without response.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had the attendant reply, "I have not eaten for many days, yet still without response.

sentences.zh: 比來中外貴賤，皆言四郊有雨，朕疑其欲相寬勉，未必有實。

translations.literal: Recently inside and outside, noble and base alike, all say the four suburbs have rain — I suspect they wish to comfort me and that it is not necessarily real.
translations.idiomatic: Recently everyone inside and outside the court, noble and base alike, has said that rain has fallen in the four suburbs. I suspect they wish only to comfort me and that it may not be real.

sentences.zh: 方將遣使視之，果如所言，即當進膳；

translations.literal: I am about to send an envoy to inspect; if it is truly as they say, I will at once resume meals;
translations.idiomatic: I am about to send an envoy to inspect. If it is truly as they say, I will at once resume my meals;

sentences.zh: 如其不然，朕何以生為！

translations.literal: if it is not so, how can I go on living!
translations.idiomatic: if it is not so, how can I go on living!

sentences.zh: 當以身為萬民塞咎耳！」

translations.literal: I ought to use my body to bear the fault for the ten thousand people!"
translations.idiomatic: I ought to use my own body to bear the fault for the ten thousand people!"

sentences.zh: 是夕，大雨。

translations.literal: That evening, heavy rain fell.
translations.idiomatic: That evening, heavy rain fell.

sentences.zh: 魏太子恂不好學，體素肥大，苦河南地熱，常思北歸。

translations.literal: Wei crown prince Xun did not love learning; his constitution was always large and fat; he suffered from the heat of the Henan region and often thought of returning north.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei crown prince Xun did not love learning. His constitution was naturally large and heavy, he suffered from the heat of the Henan region, and he often thought of returning north.

sentences.zh: 魏主賜之衣冠，徇常私著胡服。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler bestowed robes and caps on him, but Xun habitually wore barbarian dress in private.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei ruler bestowed robes and caps on him, but Xun habitually wore barbarian dress in private.

sentences.zh: 中庶子遼東高道悅數切諫，恂惡之。

translations.literal: Central Palace Attendant Gao Daoyue of Liaodong repeatedly remonstrated bluntly; Xun hated him.
translations.idiomatic: The Central Palace Attendant Gao Daoyue of Liaodong remonstrated bluntly again and again; Xun came to hate him.

sentences.zh: 八月，戊戌，帝如嵩高，恂與左右密謀，召牧馬輕騎奔平城，手刃道悅於禁中。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on wuxu, the emperor went to Song Gao. Xun secretly plotted with his close attendants, summoned horse-herders and light cavalry to flee to Pingcheng, and personally slew Daoyue in the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on wuxu, the emperor went to Mount Song. Xun secretly plotted with his close attendants, summoned horse-herders and light cavalry to flee to Pingcheng, and personally slew Daoyue in the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 領軍無儼勒門防遏，入夜乃定。

translations.literal: Commandant of the Guards Wu Yan secured the gates and blocked access; only by night was order restored.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant of the Guards Wu Yan secured the gates and held them closed; order was restored only after nightfall.

sentences.zh: 詰旦，尚書陸琇馳以啟帝，帝大駭，秘其事，仍至汴口而還。

translations.literal: At dawn, Master of Writing Lu Xiu rode in haste to inform the emperor. The emperor was greatly alarmed, kept the matter secret, and still went to Bian Ford before returning.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn, Master of Writing Lu Xiu rode posthaste to report to the emperor. The emperor was greatly alarmed, kept the affair secret, and nevertheless went on to Bian Ford before returning.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，入宮，引見恂，數其罪，親與咸陽王禧等更代杖之百餘下，扶曳出外，囚於城西；

translations.literal: On jiayin he entered the palace, summoned Xun, enumerated his crimes, and personally with Prince Xi of Xianyang and others took turns beating him more than a hundred blows, had him supported and dragged outside, and imprisoned him west of the city;
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin he entered the palace, summoned Xun, and enumerated his crimes. He personally took turns with Prince Xi of Xianyang and others in beating him more than a hundred blows, had him supported and dragged outside, and imprisoned him west of the city;

sentences.zh: 月餘乃能起。

translations.literal: Only after more than a month could he rise.
translations.idiomatic: More than a month passed before he could rise.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，魏相州刺史南安惠王楨卒。

translations.literal: On dingsi, Prince Zhen of Nan'an the Kind, Wei inspector of Xiang province, died.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi, Prince Zhen of Nan'an the Kind, Wei inspector of Xiang province, died.

sentences.zh: 九月，戊辰，魏主講武於小平津；

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on wuchen, the Wei ruler reviewed troops at Xiaoping Ford;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on wuchen, the Wei ruler held a military review at Xiaoping Ford;

sentences.zh: 癸酉，還宮。

translations.literal: On guiyou, he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou, he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，戊戌，魏詔：「軍士自代來者，皆以為羽林、虎賁。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, on wuxu, a Wei edict: "Soldiers coming from Dai are all to be made Feathered Forest guards and tiger guards.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on wuxu, a Wei edict declared: "Soldiers coming from Dai are all to be made Feathered Forest guards and tiger guards.

sentences.zh: 司州民十二夫調一，吏以供公私力役。」

translations.literal: For every twelve commoner households in Sizhou one [household] is levied in rotation, the clerks supplying public and private corvée labor."
translations.idiomatic: In Sizhou, one household in every twelve was levied in rotation, the clerks supplying labor for public and private service."

sentences.zh: 魏吐京胡反，詔朔州刺史元彬行汾州事，帥並、肆之眾以討之。

translations.literal: The Tujing Hu of Wei rebelled. An edict ordered Shuozhou Inspector Yuan Bin to act for Bingzhou and lead the forces of Bing and Si to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: The Tujing Hu of Wei rebelled. An edict ordered Shuozhou Inspector Yuan Bin to administer Bingzhou affairs and lead the forces of Bing and Si to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 彬，楨之子也。

translations.literal: Bin was Zhen's son.
translations.idiomatic: Bin was Zhen's son.

sentences.zh: 彬遣統軍奚康生擊叛胡，破之，追至車突谷，又破之，俘雜畜以萬數。

translations.literal: Bin sent Commander-in-Chief Xi Kangsheng to strike the rebel Hu, defeated them, pursued to Chetu Valley, defeated them again, and captured mixed livestock by the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Bin sent Commander-in-Chief Xi Kangsheng to attack the rebel Hu, defeated them, pursued them to Chetu Valley, defeated them again, and captured tens of thousands of mixed livestock.

sentences.zh: 詔以彬為汾州刺史。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Bin Bingzhou inspector.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Bin Bingzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 胡去居等六百餘人保險不服，彬請兵二萬以討之，有司奏許之，魏主大怒曰：「小寇何有發兵之理！

translations.literal: Hu Quju and more than six hundred others held strong positions and would not submit. Bin requested twenty thousand troops to campaign against them; the relevant offices memorialized assent. The Wei ruler was greatly angry and said, "What reason is there to dispatch troops for such petty bandits!
translations.idiomatic: Hu Quju and more than six hundred others held defensible ground and refused submission. Bin requested twenty thousand troops to campaign against them; the relevant offices memorialized approval. The Wei ruler was furious and said, "What reason is there to dispatch troops for such petty bandits!

sentences.zh: 可隨宜討治。

translations.literal: Deal with them as circumstances require.
translations.idiomatic: Deal with them as circumstances require.

sentences.zh: 若不能克，必須大兵者，則先斬刺史，然後發兵！」

translations.literal: If you cannot subdue them and truly need a great army, first behead the inspector — and only then dispatch troops!"
translations.idiomatic: If you cannot subdue them and truly need a large army, first behead the inspector — and only then dispatch troops!"

sentences.zh: 彬大懼，督帥州兵，身先將士，討去居，平之。

translations.literal: Bin was greatly afraid; he supervised and led the provincial troops, himself going ahead of the soldiers, attacked Quju, and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Bin was terrified. He supervised the provincial troops, took the lead before his soldiers, attacked Quju, and pacified the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 魏主引見群臣於清徽堂，議廢太子恂。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler summoned the ministers at Qinghui Hall to deliberate on deposing Crown Prince Xun.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei ruler summoned the ministers at Qinghui Hall to deliberate on deposing Crown Prince Xun.

sentences.zh: 太子太傅穆亮、少保李沖免冠頓首謝。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Grand Tutor Mu Liang and Junior Guardian Li Chong removed their caps and kowtowed in apology.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Grand Tutor Mu Liang and Junior Guardian Li Chong removed their caps and kowtowed in apology.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿所謝者私也，我所議者國也！

translations.literal: The emperor said, "What you apologize for is private; what I deliberate is the state!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "What you apologize for is a private matter; what I deliberate is the state!

sentences.zh: 『大義滅親』，古人所貴。

translations.literal: 'Destroying kin for the greater righteousness' — the ancients prized this.
translations.idiomatic: "Destroying kin for the greater righteousness" — the ancients prized this.

sentences.zh: 今恂欲違父逃叛，跨據恆、朔，天下之惡孰大焉！

translations.literal: Now Xun wishes to defy his father and flee in rebellion, to hold Heng and Shuo crosswise — what evil in the realm is greater!
translations.idiomatic: Now Xun wishes to defy his father and flee in rebellion, to seize and hold Heng and Shuo — what evil in the realm is greater!

sentences.zh: 若不去之，乃社稷之憂也。」

translations.literal: If he is not removed, it will be a worry for the altars of state."
translations.idiomatic: If he is not removed, it will be a calamity for the altars of state."

sentences.zh: 閏月，丙寅，廢恂為庶人，置於河陽無鼻城，以兵守之，服食所供，粗免饑寒而已。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on bingyin, Xun was deposed as a commoner and placed in Wubi City at Heyang, with soldiers guarding him; what was supplied for food and clothing scarcely spared him hunger and cold.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on bingyin, Xun was deposed to commoner status and placed in Wubi City at Heyang under military guard; what was supplied for food and clothing barely kept hunger and cold at bay.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，魏置常平倉。

translations.literal: On wuchen, Wei established Ever-Normal Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen, Wei established Ever-Normal Granaries.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，太子寶卷冠。

translations.literal: On wuyin, Crown Prince Baojuan received the capping ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin, Crown Prince Baojuan received the capping ceremony.

sentences.zh: 初，魏文明太后欲廢魏主，穆泰切諫而止，由是有寵。

translations.literal: Initially when Empress Dowager Wencheng of Wei wished to depose the Wei ruler, Mu Tai remonstrated bluntly and stopped it; thereupon he enjoyed favor.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Empress Dowager Wencheng of Wei wished to depose the Wei ruler, Mu Tai remonstrated bluntly and stopped it; from that time he enjoyed favor.

sentences.zh: 及帝南遷洛陽，所親任者多中州儒士，宗室及代人往往不樂。

translations.literal: When the emperor moved the capital south to Luoyang, those he trusted and employed were mostly Central Plains Confucian scholars; the imperial house and the people of Dai often were displeased.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor moved the capital south to Luoyang, those he trusted and employed were mostly Central Plains Confucian scholars; members of the imperial house and the people of Dai were often displeased.

sentences.zh: 泰自尚書右僕射出為定州刺史，自陳久病，土溫則甚，乞為恆州；

translations.literal: Tai left office as Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing to become Dingzhou inspector; he himself declared chronic illness, that warm soil aggravated it severely, and begged for Hengzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Tai left his post as Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing to become Dingzhou inspector. He declared chronic illness, saying warm soil aggravated it severely, and begged to be transferred to Hengzhou;

sentences.zh: 帝為之徙恆州刺史陸睿為定州，以泰代之。

translations.literal: The emperor moved Hengzhou Inspector Lu Rui to Dingzhou for him and had Tai replace him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor moved Hengzhou Inspector Lu Rui to Dingzhou for his sake and had Tai replace him.

sentences.zh: 泰至，睿未發，遂相與謀作亂，陰結鎮北大將軍樂陵王思譽、安樂侯隆、撫冥鎮將魯郡侯業、驍騎將軍超等，共推朔州刺史陽平王熙為主。

translations.literal: When Tai arrived, Rui had not yet departed; they then plotted rebellion together, secretly joining General Who Guards the North Siyu of Leling, Marquis Long of Anle, Commander of Fuoming Garrison Marquis Ye of Lu Commandery, Valiant Cavalry General Chao, and others to make Shuo Inspector Prince Xi of Yangping their lord.
translations.idiomatic: When Tai arrived, Rui had not yet departed. They then plotted rebellion together, secretly winning over General Who Guards the North Siyu of Leling, Marquis Long of Anle, Commander of Fuoming Garrison Marquis Ye of Lu Commandery, Valiant Cavalry General Chao, and others to make Shuo Inspector Prince Xi of Yangping their leader.

sentences.zh: 思譽，天賜之子；

translations.literal: Siyu was the son of Tianci;
translations.idiomatic: Siyu was the son of Tianci;

sentences.zh: 業，丕之弟；

translations.literal: Ye was Pi's younger brother;
translations.idiomatic: Ye was Pi's younger brother;

sentences.zh: 隆、超，皆丕之子也。

translations.literal: Long and Chao were both sons of Pi.
translations.idiomatic: Long and Chao were both sons of Pi.

sentences.zh: 睿以為洛陽休明，勸泰緩之，泰由是未發。

translations.literal: Rui held that Luoyang was glorious and at peace and urged Tai to delay; Tai therefore did not rise.
translations.idiomatic: Rui held that Luoyang was glorious and at peace and urged Tai to delay; Tai therefore did not rise.

sentences.zh: 頤偽許泰等以安其意，而密以狀聞。
